Title: Tuanku Muhriz's return from overseas to draw attention amid Negri Sembilan throne dispute
Article:
SEREMBAN: The return of Yang di-Pertuan Besar Negri Sembilan Tuanku Muhriz Tuanku Munawir from overseas tonight is expected to draw attention amid an ongoing dispute over the state's throne.
Tuanku Muhriz is scheduled to arrive at Terminal 1 of Kuala Lumpur International Airport (KLIA) in Sepang at 8.30pm.
According to a poster circulating on social media, members of the public and several non-governmental organisations (NGOs) have been urged to gather at the Terminal 1 fifth-floor car park to welcome and show their support for the ruler.
The gathering is said to be organised by Profans, Waris Dato Siamang Gagap, Waris Negeri Sembilan and Pekan.
Tuanku Muhriz's return comes amid conflicting positions over a proclamation concerning his removal as Yang di-Pertuan Besar.
Negri Sembilan Menteri Besar Datuk Ismail Lasim
today confirmed
that a proclamation removing Tuanku Muhriz Tuanku Munawir as Yang di-Pertuan Besar Negri Sembilan had been approved.
He said the decision was unanimously endorsed by all members of the state executive council (exco) at its meeting on Tuesday.
He said the state secretary had been instructed to proceed with the gazettement of the proclamation in accordance with existing regulations.
"Today, I wish to confirm that the proclamation was discussed and unanimously decided upon by all exco members at the state executive council meeting on Tuesday.
"The gazettement process has been referred to the state secretary to proceed in accordance with existing regulations. That's all," he said.
However, the Dewan Keadilan dan Undang (DKU) Negeri Sembilan said Tuanku Muhriz remains the legitimate Yang di-Pertuan Besar.
Its secretary Raja Norazli Raja Nordin said according to Article 16 of the Laws of the State of Negri Sembilan 1959, matters related to Malay customs, including the selection, appointment, abdication, and removal from office of the Yang di-Pertuan Besar and the Undang, fall under the jurisdiction of the DKU.
He said the DKU's advice on such matters was final and cannot be challenged or questioned in any court on any grounds whatsoever.
Meanwhile, Tuanku Muhriz is scheduled to perform Friday prayers at the Royal Tuanku Munawir Mosque in Seri Menanti, Kuala Pilah, tomorrow.
A solidarity gathering for Tuanku Muhriz is also reportedly planned by NGOs at the same location after Friday prayers.

Title: Impoverished by war in Iran, Afghan migrants return to Taliban rule
Article:
MOHAMMAD Saeed had just turned 18 when he fled to Iran with his parents and younger brother and sister, escaping the Taliban's return to power in Afghanistan in 2021.
Now Saeed and his family are among thousands who have returned home to escape the economic crisis in Iran triggered by the conflict with the US and Israel.
The family came back nearly empty-handed, Saeed said.
"The Iranian currency had fallen so sharply," he said, that the family's savings, held in Iranian rials, lost over two-thirds of their value.
For decades, Iran's industrialised and much larger economy offered Afghans an escape from poverty and, in the 1990s and again since 2021, from the harsh rule of the Taliban.
Now, Iran's economy has collapsed so severely that many Afghans said they saw returning as their only option.
They are coming back with their wives and daughters, despite the severe restrictions on women in Afghanistan, with curbs on their education, travel and employment.
Reuters journalists spent one week in the border regions of Afghanistan's Herat province and neighbouring Farah speaking to people returning from Iran.
Free to discuss it without fear of Iranian government scrutiny, most of those returning described a shattered economy in Iran.
At the dusty Islam Qala border crossing between Iran and Afghanistan, a near-constant flow of returning migrants were undergoing document checks and registration formalities.
Officials were sitting in makeshift shipping containers. Coming back to their homeland, the returnees were faced with barren desert mountains and a pothole-plastered highway, the road to Herat, the biggest city in western Afghanistan.
Most returning Afghans said they had been out of work for months and crushed by spiralling inflation before they decided to return.
Compounded by the impact of tightening sanctions and a US naval blockade that has recently left Iran without shipping any meaningful crude exports through the Strait of Hormuz, consumer prices have surged by nearly 90 per cent year on year, according to Iran's Statistical Centre.
Food inflation has been even higher, at almost 130 per cent, making bread, milk and other essentials increasingly unaffordable.
In the past, some Afghan salesmen could make profits in Iran's bazaars by selling goods at around double the price at which they'd been purchased, said Sayed Jawed Qazi Khani, a 40-year-old migrant. But inflation and vanishing savings among both Iranians and Afghan migrants led to a collapse in consumer demand.
"What remained was day labour," he said, often at the same wage as one year ago.
Only 29 per cent of Afghans who recently returned from Iran said they had any savings left after their average income fell by nearly one-third compared to pre-crisis levels, according to surveys by the International Organisation for Migration (IOM).
More than two million Afghans have left Iran over the past two years. Most were deported or pressured to leave by Iranian authorities before the latest wave of returnees, who left amid the war, according to data from the UN Refugee Agency.
Forced deportation remains a leading reason why Afghans are returning, with unaccompanied men long appearing to be the primary focus of Iranian authorities.
But compared to pre-crisis levels, the crowds of returning Afghans increasingly also include women and entire families, according to returnees and IOM data.
For many Afghan mothers and their daughters who had held out in Iran after the Taliban takeover of Afghanistan, Iran's recent economic crisis has confronted them with an almost impossible choice: face poverty there, or return to a country where half the women leave home only once or twice a month, according to the UN.
[[nid:1534859]]
The Taliban's rules restrict women from travelling without male guardians and have barred them from some professions. The Taliban say they respect women's rights in accordance with Islamic syariah law.
Abdul Jabbar, 44, said he did not want to take his wife, two daughters, grandson and mother back to Afghanistan. Their family had lived in Iran for nearly four decades and Jabbar had found work as an exterior finisher of buildings.
The family had a comfortable life and a modern apartment in Kerman, near an Iranian military base.
His face flushed from the heat of the flatbread oven wedged into the one room they now have in Afghanistan, he said in an interview: "I used to say that even if Afghanistan was only two streets away, I would not go."
When the nearby military base was repeatedly hit by missiles and work dried up amid the war this year, Jabbar said, extended Afghan family members encouraged him to return, promising work and safety from American missiles.
When Jabbar arrived in Afghanistan with virtually no belongings or savings, relatives donated essentials and lent him money.
Two months on, he remains unemployed and, unable to repay the money, has worn out his welcome.
The family now lives in a sweltering mud-brick house with only one room where solar panels are the sole source of electricity. The dusty carpet was donated.
His 15-year-old daughter Setayesh, who wants to become a fashion designer, misses her life in Iran.
"If I could, I would go back," she said. "For my education, my friends."
At Islam Qala, at least 20 to 40 families, including women and girls, return voluntarily each day, said Abdul Ghani Qazizadeh, a senior Taliban government official at the border.
"The wages they earn are no longer enough to cover their basic living expenses," he said.
Many Afghan workers complained that their Iranian employers were withholding wages, he said. "Everyone complains that their money has been left behind."
In Iran, Saeed and his mother, 42-year-old Rezwana Jami, said they had started a business producing cheese used in pizzas when they arrived in 2021. Initially, it thrived, and the family found loyal customers.
As US-Iran tensions escalated this year and inflation surged, food became so scarce that Jami said she struggled to source the ingredients needed for the business, including milk.
"I could no longer continue production," she said, eventually forcing the family to return five months ago.
Jami and Saeed said they have used their last savings to buy new kitchen equipment in Afghanistan and have resumed the production of pizza cheese in their new home.
The family sees a market opportunity in Afghanistan, where high-quality pizza cheese is a rare commodity.
They say they work with girls who would be of school age in other countries, but are barred from education above sixth grade and from university under Taliban rules.
Since Jami's return to Afghanistan five months ago, she said her 17-year-old daughter has struggled the most.
"She keeps telling me, 'Mother, I studied for eight years, and now I'm just staying at home'," Jami said. "There is nothing I can do except telling her, 'Be patient. God is generous.'"
* The writers are from Reuters

Title: Rauf: DAP's choice whether they want to contest 10 or 20 seats
Article:
MASJID TANAH: It is up to DAP to choose the number of seats to contest in the Melaka election, says Chief Minister and state Barisan Nasional chairman Datuk Seri Ab Rauf Yusoh.
However, he said any decision on seat allocations will be made only after an agreement is reached between parties should negotiations take place.
He said he had no right to stop any party from voicing their intentions to contest any seat.
Rauf said, on an open political stage, every party has the right to decide on its own stand and strategy.
This, he added, included where it wanted to contest.
"If DAP wants to contest 10 or even 20 seats, it's up to them. That is their party.
"I only look after the interests of my own party and of course I will not stop them (DAP) because I do not look after the interests of other parties," he said after launching Powering Knowledge Stem Discovery @ School 2026 programme at SK Tanjung Bidara.
Rauf was commenting on DAP's intentions to contest several seats, including the Duyong constituency currently held by BN's Datuk Mohd Noor Helmy Abdul Halem.
Melaka DAP chairman Khoo Poay Tiong was reported to have said Duyong was among the seats which his party could possibly wrest.
He had said DAP also intended to defend the four seats it had won in the previous election.
In 2021, DAP's Damian Yeo Shen Li lost to Noor Helmy by a majority of just 200 votes.
The election before that, in 2018, DAP took the seat with a majority of 2,895 votes.
Rauf said the political stage was open and any party has the right to voice its intention to contest any seat.
"Any party can voice their desires. However, it is subject to negotiations between parties (if such negotiations take place)... only then can we decide (who contests where)," he said.

Title: MASkargo, IAG & Qatar Airways Cargo complete trial ahead of JV launch
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: MAB Kargo Sdn Bhd (MASkargo), IAG Cargo and Qatar Airways Cargo have completed the trial of the first customer shipment transported across all three carriers.
This is ahead of the full launch of their global cargo joint business later this year.
The shipment saw 11 tonnes of copper foil transported from Kuala Lumpur to Chicago O'Hare via Doha and Dublin.
Announced in 2025, the global cargo joint business brings together three leading cargo carriers to create a network of unprecedented scale and reach.
Once fully launched, customers will gain access to over 400 destinations across six continents and a more seamless access to global markets.
MASkargo chief executive officer (CEO) Mark Jason Thomas said the first shipment demonstrates the potential of this collaboration to strengthen the link between Asia's production centres and global demand.
"As we progress towards launch, our shared focus is on translating that potential into wider market access, greater flexibility and enduring value for our customers,"  he said in a statement.
IAG Cargo was appointed earlier this year as the ground handling agent for Qatar Airways Cargo in Dublin and Madrid, two of the joint business' strategic hubs.
Alongside the introduction of MASkargo handling operations at London Heathrow last year, these developments have supported the operational integration required to deliver the joint business.
"Alongside our partners, we have been aligning our operations, systems and expertise to create a joint business that works seamlessly across our combined networks.
"As we progress towards full launch, our focus remains on delivering a coordinated proposition that provides tangible benefits for customers across the global air freight market,"  said IAG Cargo CEO David Shepherd.
Qatar Airways Cargo chief officer cargo Mark Drusch said the tripartite shipment showcased the operational alignment, connectivity and customer-focused approach that will underpin the joint business.
"For our customers, this is about creating a simpler, more connected experience and demonstrates the strength of our collaboration.
"By combining our complementary networks and expertise, we are building a truly global cargo offering that delivers greater reach, more routing flexibility and enhanced efficiency," he added.

Title: Court grants GISBH-linked businessman DNAA in intimidation case
Article:
PUTRAJAYA: The magistrates' court today granted businessman Mohamad Riza Makar, who is linked to Global Ikhwan Service and Business Holdings (GISBH), a discharge not amounting to an acquittal (DNAA) in an intimidation case.
The decision came after deputy public prosecutor Faizah Khalilah Zaberi told magistrate Irza Zulaikha Rohanuddin that the prosecution wanted to review the case further.
Riza, 41, had pleaded not guilty in 2024 to allegedly intimidating a 25-year-old woman into withdrawing a police report lodged against the company. He allegedly committed the offence at a parking lot in Presint 4 at 10pm on Sept 9 the same year.
He was accused of threatening her by saying: "Kita tunggu... Kita tahu dekat mana rumah, suami dan keluarga" ("We will wait... We know where your house, husband and family are").
The charge framed under Section 506 of the Penal Code carries a jail term up to two years or a fine or both upon conviction.
Outside the courtroom, Riza's lawyers, Shahruddin Othman and Boestamam Ahmad, said they had applied for a full acquittal after the complainant failed to appear in court today and at an earlier hearing on Aug 27.
"We asked the court to fully acquit our client because the complainant failed to appear at both proceedings.
"The complainant had already given her testimony but the prosecution wanted to recall her.
"However, she failed to appear on both occasions," said Boestamam.
He said the defence had argued that continuing the case would be a waste of time while the prosecution maintained that it wanted to review the charge.
"The magistrate granted the prosecution's application for a DNAA," he said.
A DNAA releases an accused from a charge but does not amount to a full acquittal.
The accused may be charged again over the same alleged offence.
Meanwhile, Riza said he was grateful to God that he had not been convicted after nearly two years of court proceedings and pressure.
He said the case had affected his personal life, reputation, family, employment and finances.
"I hope the public understands that I have gone through the legal process and that I should no longer be associated with these accusations as though I had been found guilty. I believe the truth will prevail," he said.
Riza added that he was considering legal action against the complainant to seek justice and protect his reputation and that of his family.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: 12-year-old faces possible PwD registration after alleged bullying leaves her near paralysis
Article:
PADANG BESAR: A 12-year-old schoolgirl who has been bedridden and almost paralysed following alleged bullying at school now faces another difficult chapter, with doctors recommending that she be registered as a Person with Disabilities (PwD).
Her mother, Norasikin Hasin, 32, said the hospital recently issued a confirmation letter to facilitate the registration of her eldest daughter following a deterioration in her physical condition.
Norasikin said she was torn over whether to proceed with the registration as her daughter was born healthy and had grown up actively like other children.
"What mother would not be heartbroken? My daughter was born healthy and excelled, but her life changed in an instant because of bullying.
"To this day, I am still torn over whether to register her as a PwD because it is difficult to accept what has happened to her," she said when contacted.
Norasikin said her daughter had been unable to attend school for almost eight months since the incident in February due to her health condition.
She also expressed disappointment with the school administration and the state Education Department (JPN), which she alleged had failed to provide any updates or assistance regarding her daughter's condition.
"I am deeply disappointed because, until now, the authorities seem to have turned a blind eye.
"No JPN representative has come to visit her, while the school principal has remained silent without providing any explanation or showing any concern," she said.
It was reported previously that the girl had been
diagnosed with post-traumatic stress disorder
(PTSD) and was suffering from severe mobility problems, allegedly following bullying at school.
The bullying involved physical and psychological abuse by her schoolmates at a primary school here, including an incident in which her chair was pulled away as she was about to sit in class.
Norasikin first noticed changes in her daughter's physical and emotional condition in February, when the girl began frequently complaining of back pain and showed significant behavioural changes, including withdrawing from others and spending more time lying down whenever she returned home during school breaks.

Title: North Korea says US-led arms buildup justifies expanding nuclear force
Article:
BEIJING: North Korea's vice defence minister said on Thursday that a growing US-led military buildup and what he called an expanding nuclear alliance among Washington, Seoul and Tokyo justified Pyongyang's efforts to strengthen and expand its nuclear forces.
Speaking at the Beijing Xiangshan Forum, China's flagship international security conference, Vice Defence Minister Kim Kang Il said North Korea's status as a nuclear weapons state was irreversible and pledged to continue expanding its nuclear arsenal.
"The ceaseless nuclear arms buildup of the enemy states fully justifies the building of a solid nuclear shield of the DPRK," Kim said, using the acronym for North Korea's formal name, the Democratic People's Republic of Korea.
"As the enemy states' nuclear threat reaches the extreme level ... the DPRK will firmly defend the peace and stability in the Korean Peninsula and the region by ceaselessly expanding and strengthening its self-defensive nuclear deterrent."
Kim blamed tensions on the Korean Peninsula on what he called Washington's "invariable" hostile policy toward North Korea and accused the United States of turning trilateral cooperation with South Korea and Japan into a nuclear alliance.
He said North Korea's constitutional status as a nuclear weapons state was "the line of no retreat" and urged other countries to abandon what he called the "daydream" of denuclearisation.
Kim's appearance at the Xiangshan Forum marked a rare high-profile showing by North Korea at an international security gathering in recent years and came as Pyongyang seeks closer ties with Beijing amid tensions with Washington and its allies.
Asked about the possibility of a meeting between U.S. President Donald Trump and North Korean leader Kim Jong Un, Kim said he was not in a position to discuss whether such a summit could take place.
Former U.S. Special Representative for North Korea Stephen Biegun said at the Korea Risk Group's West Coast Exchange conference on Thursday that North Korea's muted response to Trump's repeated claims of communication with Kim Jong Un suggested Pyongyang was "not closing the door" on potential future talks with Washington.
Biegun said it "would not be a surprise at all" if Trump were to propose a meeting with the North Korean leader following the APEC summit in China in November and that such a meeting could even take place in Pyongyang.
The North Korean official's remarks followed a statement on Thursday morning from Kim Yo Jong, the powerful sister of Kim Jong Un, rejecting renewed international calls for North Korea's denuclearisation following discussions at the annual meeting of the International Atomic Energy Agency.
In a statement carried by state media KCNA, she said North Korea's status as a nuclear weapons state was "absolute" and could not be reversed, dismissing repeated denuclearisation demands as annual "noise" and insisting Pyongyang's nuclear position had been permanently established "physically and legally."
Her comments echoed a separate statement on Wednesday by a North Korean defence ministry spokesman, who accused the United States and South Korea of escalating military confrontation through joint weapons-of-mass-destruction response planning and exercises.
The spokesman said recent US-South Korean WMD response discussions amounted to an "open declaration of confrontation" and warned such actions could require Pyongyang to invoke provisions of its nuclear force policy law.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: High Court sets Nov 6 mention for Rosmah solar appeal update
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: High Court proceedings to record additional evidence from a key prosecution witness in Datin Seri Rosmah Mansor's Sarawak solar hybrid project corruption case appeal have been postponed.
The deferment follows the Court of Appeal's decision today to allow the prosecution's application to stay execution of its Sept 1 order pending an appeal to the Federal Court.
Lawyer Datuk Akberdin Abdul Kader, representing the wife of the former prime minister, informed High Court Judge Datuk Aslam Zainuddin that the defence did not object to the stay after discussions between both parties and the prosecution's filing of a certificate of urgency to expedite the apex court hearing.
He said the Court of Appeal had set Oct 7 for case management via e-Review to track the status of the Federal Court appeal, while vacating the main appeal hearing originally scheduled for October.
"Therefore, proceedings before Your Honour today will be postponed until the appeal at the Federal Court is disposed of.
"The Court of Appeal has fixed Oct 7 for case management, and we are unsure whether the Federal Court appeal can be heard before that date," he said, requesting a new case management date at the High Court.
Deputy public prosecutor Mohamad Mustaffa P. Kunyalam confirmed the postponement until the prosecution's appeal is decided.
"We request another mention date be fixed before Your Honour for this matter," he said, adding that no date has been set by the Federal Court, but the prosecution will seek the earliest available slot.
Aslam fixed Nov 6 for mention for parties to update the court on the status of the Federal Court appeal.
On Sept 1, the Court of Appeal allowed Rosmah's application to adduce additional evidence in her appeal against her conviction and sentence.
A three-member panel led by Datuk Azhahari Kamal Ramli, alongside Datuk Dr Choo Kah Sing and K. Muniandy, ordered that the additional evidence involving 16th prosecution witness Rayyan Radzwill Abdullah be recorded at the High Court within two weeks.
Following the decision, the prosecution filed a notice of appeal on Sept 4 to challenge the ruling at the Federal Court.
Rayyan, a key prosecution witness, alleged in a statutory declaration submitted as part of the additional evidence that he was pressured by the prosecution during the trial and presented documentary material challenging the credibility of his testimony.
On Sept 1, 2022, the High Court convicted Rosmah on three corruption charges under Section 16(a)(A) of the Malaysian Anti-Corruption Commission (MACC) Act 2009.
She was found guilty of soliciting RM187.5 million and receiving RM6.5 million from former Jepak Holdings managing director Saidi Abang Samsudin through her former aide, Datuk Rizal Mansor.
The gratification was an inducement to assist Jepak Holdings in securing a RM1.25 billion hybrid solar project from the Education Ministry to supply electricity to 369 rural schools in Sarawak.
Rosmah was sentenced to 10 years' jail for each charge, to run concurrently, and fined RM970 million. She was granted a stay of execution pending appeal.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: 43 countries call on Taliban to lift 'suffocating restrictions' on Afghan women
Article:
NEW YORK: More than 40 countries on Wednesday called on the Taliban government to immediately remove all restrictions on the rights of women and girls in Afghanistan.
Last month marked five years since the Taliban returned to power and imposed what the UN called "suffocating restrictions" on Afghans, especially women.
Around 2.4 million Afghan girls and young women are currently deprived of secondary education, according to Unesco.
"Since August 2021, the Taliban have implemented a policy of gender-based segregation, virtually erasing women and girls from public life and severely restricting their access to education, healthcare and employment," said Jerome Bonnafont, France's representative to the UN, speaking on behalf of the 43 signatory countries.
They include numerous European countries, as well as Liberia, the United Arab Emirates, Mexico and Japan.
"Women who refuse or are perceived to refuse to comply with these restrictions face arrest and arbitrary detention," Bonnafort continued, speaking ahead of a Security Council meeting on the situation.
"Their supporters and perceived critics of the Taliban rule also face detention and reprisals."
The signatories urged Taliban authorities "to immediately lift all restrictions on the rights of women and girls, in all their diversity, and to put an end to all human rights violations."
Despite the country's dire humanitarian situation, with much of the population living in poverty, forced returns to Afghanistan are continuing.
More than 400,000 Afghans have been forcibly returned this year, according to the United Nations, primarily from Iran and Pakistan.

Title: Loke: Negri exco members should resign if they no longer recognise Tuanku Muhriz
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Negri Sembilan executive council (exco) members should step down if they no longer recognise Tuanku Muhriz Tuanku Munawir as the state's Yang di-Pertuan Besar, DAP secretary-general Anthony Loke said.
Loke said all the exco members concerned had only recently taken their oaths of office before Tuanku Muhriz early last month.
"On the principles of integrity and dignity, if they no longer recognise him (Tuanku Muhriz) as the Yang di-Pertuan Besar of Negri Sembilan, they should resign from their respective positions," he said in a statement today.
Loke, who is also the Seremban member of Parliament, said the decision by all state exco members to recognise a successor with immediate effect was legally unfounded and could be regarded as an act of disloyalty towards the state ruler.
He said an exco decision could not, by itself, override the Constitution of Negri Sembilan 1959 or the decisions of the Negri Sembilan Dewan Keadilan dan Undang.
"If such action had been taken by the exco when Negri Sembilan was under the Pakatan Harapan government, those who have long been fond of exploiting 3R issues to blame DAP would certainly have condemned it outright.
"More regrettably, most of the exco members concerned were only recently appointed.
"Some of them have never attended a sitting of the state assembly as exco members," Loke said.
He said they should first examine and understand the relevant legal provisions and their legal authority before issuing statements concerning the position of the state ruler.
He said the Yang di-Pertuan Besar could not be removed from the throne arbitrarily without a lawful process under the Negri Sembilan Constitution.
He said the exco's action in making such an announcement had confused and undermined the orderly administration of the state and tarnished the dignity of the institution of the Yang di-Pertuan Besar.
The supremacy of the law and the dignity of the royal institution must be upheld and must not be manipulated for any political or personal interests, he said.
Earlier today, Negri Sembilan Menteri Besar Datuk I
smail Lasim
confirmed that a proclamation removing Tuanku Muhriz Tuanku Munawir as Yang di-Pertuan Besar of Negri Sembilan had been approved.
He said the decision was unanimously endorsed by all exco members at its meeting yesterday.
Yesterday, a statement issued in the name of the state exco and published by several portals said the proclamation dated April 19, 2026, concerning the selection of Tuanku Nadzaruddin Tuanku Ja'afar under Article 11 of the Laws of the Constitution of Negri Sembilan 1959 (UUTKNS), had been signed and sealed by the legitimate Undang.
The statement said the proclamation was in order and duly completed in accordance with the UUTKNS 1959.
It also said the state executive council respected the decision of the Undang Yang Empat and their prerogative powers as provided for under custom and the UUTKNS 1959.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Japan's Takaichi keeps key ministers in cabinet reshuffle
Article:
TOKYO: Japanese Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi retained her key ministers on Thursday in a cabinet reshuffle aimed at solidifying the ruling coalition and advancing a food tax cut despite concerns over how it will be financed.
Prime ministers in Japan routinely shuffle their cabinets to refresh the government's public image and to distribute ministerial posts to loyal supporters and experienced lawmakers from the same party.
But Takaichi – who has unusually high approval ratings nearly a year into office – kept core members of her team, according to a cabinet list announced by her righthand man and top government spokesman Minoru Kihara.
They include Kihara, finance minister Satsuki Katayama, foreign minister Toshimitsu Motegi and defence minister Shinjiro Koizumi.
The prime minister also retained key economic ministers, including trade and industry minister Ryosei Akazawa, who has led Japan's tariff negotiations with the United States, and economic growth strategy minister Minoru Kiuchi, who favours active fiscal spending.
Under finance minister Katayama, Japan has repeatedly intervened in the foreign exchange market to prop up the falling yen, including a rare joint intervention with the United States.
The small-scale reshuffle comes as Takaichi navigates rising inflation and a weak yen while pursuing a consumption tax cut on food starting next year.
While Takaichi's tax cut pledge is popular among voters, economists have criticised the plan, warning that she has failed to identify around five trillion yen (US$32 billion) needed annually to fund it.
Takaichi's policy of expansive government spending has also rattled the markets, pushing Japan's benchmark bond yield to around 3.0 per cent, its highest level in three decades.
On defence, Koizumi remains tasked with updating Japan's foundational national defence strategy documents alongside implementing a push to expand defence spending.
"Revising our strategy is something that has a major impact on Japan's security and on the entire region," Koizumi told reporters after he was reappointed.
He said the defence ministry "must marshal all our resources and move forward with a greater speed" with the review with "a strong sense of urgency."
Takaichi also assigned the post of minister in charge of regulatory reform to Hiroshi Nakatsuka, 70, a member of the LDP's coalition partner Japan Innovation Party.
The JIP formed a ruling alliance with Takaichi's conservative Liberal Democratic Party in October, but until now had chosen not to join her cabinet.
The premier will hold a press conference later in the day after the reshuffled Takaichi cabinet is formally launched following an attestation ceremony at the Imperial Palace.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: 102-year-old Tok Saimah shares secrets to long, healthy life
Article:
KLUANG: At 102, Saimah Sajiman still follows the simple routines that have shaped her life, particularly when it comes to her diet and regular meal times.
More fondly known as Tok Saimah, the centenarian from Kampung Rahmat, Sri Lalang, believes that maintaining a healthy diet, particularly choosing boiled food over fried or oily dishes, is among the practices that have helped her stay healthy.
"It is not that I do not eat fried food, but I prefer boiled food such as sayur bening (clear vegetable soup), ikan pais (steamed fish with spices) and traditional village ulam (vegetable salads)," she said at her residence yesterday.
Born in 1924, Tok Saimah, who was active in gardening when she was younger, said she also strictly observes her meal times, having breakfast, lunch and dinner at almost the same time every day.
"For breakfast, I will have something light to line the stomach, usually before the Dhuha prayer between 8am and 9am. Lunch is before Zohor prayer and dinner is before Isyak prayer," she said.
Her daughter, Fatimah Surip, 78, said she was grateful that her mother remained in good health and was still able to stand while performing prayers, despite having more than 20 grandchildren and 50 great-grandchildren.
"My mother does not suffer from chronic diseases, just a slight hearing problem. If you want to converse, you have to speak a little louder, and she prefers using a wheelchair to move from one place to another," she said.
Tok Saimah recently gained attention on social media after receiving a visit from Her Majesty Raja Zarith Sofiah, Queen of Malaysia, last Sunday.
Fatimah said her mother's age and experiences of living through several eras, including the Japanese occupation, British colonial rule and the communist insurgency, were among the things that drew Her Majesty's attention during the visit.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Give parents a middle ground on haze absences, say parents, school groups
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Parents and school community leaders want the Education Ministry to have a middle ground option when it comes to keeping their children home because of the haze.
While Education Minister Datuk Seri Fadhlina Sidek has said
parents may keep children home
during haze without penalty, they said this still left parents choosing between their children's health and education.
SK Convent Ipoh Parent-Teacher Association chairman Datuk Seri Razlan Yusuf said this was the case as schools still remained open regardless of whether a child is absent due to the haze.
He proposed that optional attendance in view of air quality issues be combined with home-based learning so that children being kept home by their parents would not lose out on their education.
He also said there should be clearer communication from schools on Air Pollutant Index readings and learning arrangements.
Razlan, who has two children, aged 8 and 12, attending the school, also called for flexibility, saying that schools should not need to wait for the API threshold to surpass 200 to close.
Any reading between 201 and 300 is considered very unhealthy, while anything 301 and above is considered hazardous.
A mother of two who only wanted to be identified as Azua said the ministry's standard operating procedures should be revised to provide clearer and more specific guidelines based on the severity of the haze, including clear API thresholds for reducing outdoor activities, temporary school closure or online learning.
"Schools should also be given sufficient flexibility to protect students when conditions worsen," she said.
Another mother who only wanted to be identified as Nadira said, as her daughter in kindergarten has asthma, the distinction between thresholds is not abstract.
Her daughter, under paediatric follow-up measures at Putrajaya Hospital since she was young, started coughing after being sent to school during a week when the API reading in her area passed 140.
"I don't want it to get worse because she has to go to the hospital many times because of her asthma," said Nadira, adding that she kept her daughter home once symptoms began.
She said the teacher had told her the child need not attend when unwell, and that an inhaler is used daily at home.
Normaya Othman, however, said she will keep sending her 8-year-old daughter to school unless the Education Ministry orders a closure.
She said, though, that she has limited her daughter's outdoor activities, while requiring her to wear a mask.
"Unless the school or the Education Ministry officially announces closure, I would prefer to send her to school as usual," she said, adding that parents need clearer, more timely guidance once air quality turns unhealthy, since deciding without a clear announcement is difficult.
Datuk Saniboey Mohd Ismail, whose children are still in school and university, said the responsibility for deciding on outdoor activities during haze should fall on the ministry, not parents.
"It is not about my personal opinion, It is about what decision the Education Ministry makes on the haze issue.
"I want my child to learn and be healthy," he said, adding that parents who kept children home risked being blamed later if the children fell behind.
Under the National Haze Action Plan, outdoor school activities are suspended once the API readings exceed 100, while schools close once readings pass 200.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Buckingham Palace hits back at claims in Princess Diana book
Article:
LONDON: Buckingham Palace has hit back at claims by the late Princess Diana's brother that King Charles III acted insensitively following her death in a car crash almost 30 years ago.
The palace issued an unusually strong statement after Charles Spencer claimed in his new memoir that the then-prince, Diana's former husband, said "rest assured, we'll forget her soon enough" days after she died in 1997.
"While we do not comment on books as a matter of principle," a palace spokesperson said late Wednesday.
"His Majesty is mindful that the pain of fraternal grief can cloud reason, affect judgment and colour memory in ways others do not recognise, even many years after such a loss."
"Swan Song: Diana, My Sister" is due to be published next week.
In the book, serialised in the Daily Mail, Spencer claims that Charles subjected him to a "stream of anger" after he insisted Diana would not have wanted her sons, princes William and Harry, then aged 15 and 12, to walk in her funeral procession.
"He unleashed down the phone what I have always taken to be his pent-up contempt for Diana, and his horror that the world was so bowled over by her death. 'Rest assured', he hissed, 'we'll forget her soon enough!'," Spencer writes.
Diana, who was extremely popular in the UK, died in Paris at the age of 36 after the car she was travelling in crashed as it tried to get away from paparazzi photographers.
Her death sparked an outpouring of grief in Britain and led to accusations that the monarchy failed to show the appropriate empathy.
UK media likened the language in the palace's statement to the late Queen Elizabeth II's response in 2021 to claims of racism in the royal family from Harry and his wife Meghan.
The queen said that "some recollections may vary."
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Malacca Strait cable disruption could cripple key services across the region
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Beneath the Strait of Malacca, one of the world's busiest shipping routes, lie strategically critical submarine cables transmitting US$10 trillion in financial transactions daily, with any serious disruption potentially crippling banks, hospitals and airports in Malaysia and across the region.
Citizens International chairman Dr Shahridan Faiez, who is also Technical Director at Think City and previously worked with the World Bank, said the submarine cables added another critical dimension to the strategic importance of the waterway, which is already a major conduit for global trade and energy supplies.
Speaking in an interview on Bernama TV's programme Bernama World on Wednesday, he said more than 39 per cent of seaborne oil passed through the waterway while nearly 80 per cent of East Asia's oil imports came through it, with an annual cargo value of US$5 trillion.
"What many people are not familiar with is the fact that underneath the water, on the seabed, are very important and strategically critical submarine cables that carry data, and these submarine cables transmit US$10 trillion of financial transactions every day.
"If anything negative were to happen to these submarine cables in the Strait of Malacca, it would have a huge impact not simply on our energy security, but on the running of our banks, hospitals, airports and basically, it would cripple the operation of not just our country, but also the region as a whole," he said.
Citizens International is a Malaysian-based international NGO advocating peaceful coexistence and global cooperation.
On the possibility of diverting shipping through the Lombok and Makassar straits if the Strait of Malacca were seriously disrupted, Shahridan said such an option was not realistic, given the significant difference in vessel traffic and the lack of necessary infrastructure.
"It is actually not a fair comparison, because the Strait of Malacca has over 102,000 transits a year. In contrast, Lombok and Makassar have only about 6,000 vessels, which is less than six per cent of the traffic going through the Strait of Malacca. So expecting that to be a backup plan is not realistic," he said.
He said the Lombok and Makassar straits also lacked the necessary infrastructure to serve as alternative shipping routes, including ports, bunkering and pilot services, as well as ship repair yards.
Compounding the vulnerability, Shahridan said only about 20 of the 60 specialised cable repair ships worldwide were operational at any one time, meaning repairs following an incident in the Strait of Malacca could take months rather than weeks and have a major impact on Malaysia and the region.
Against this backdrop, he said the Strait of Hormuz crisis should serve as a wake-up call for Southeast Asia as any disruption to the Strait of Malacca could affect not only energy security but also critical data and financial transactions.
On the security of the waterway, Shahridan said primary responsibility must stay strictly with the littoral states, namely Malaysia, Indonesia, Singapore and Thailand.
He said an external power had proposed playing a role in policing the Strait of Malacca in the early 2000s but the proposal was rejected by the littoral states and Asean, which subsequently developed the Malacca Straits Patrol.
"We want to maintain that. We don't want any of the big powers to muscle their way into the Strait of Malacca.
"Keeping the neutrality of our zone and region is very important, and this is where the role of Asean becomes critical while the concept of Asean centrality really has to be put into practice," he said.
On whether Asean needed a more binding framework to protect the Strait of Malacca, he said Asean already had the Treaty of Amity and Cooperation (TAC), established in 1976, which solidified the principles of non-interference and peaceful settlement of disputes and conflicts.  –BERNAMA
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Room view complaint escalates into assault at Bukit Bintang hotel
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: A China tourist's request to change her hotel room over its view turned chaotic after she claimed she was assaulted and injured by a local married couple in the hotel lobby in Bukit Bintang here yesterday.
The woman, who has been travelling alone in Malaysia since Sept 9, had gone to the hotel's front desk to request a room change after she was dissatisfied with the view from her original room.
According to her account, the request was rejected by hotel staff, who she claimed also appeared displeased.
A source said the woman became unhappy with the treatment and got into a heated argument with the hotel staff.
"However, during the argument, the victim claimed she was suddenly confronted by a local married couple, which caught her by surprise.
"Although she claimed she had not provoked the couple, another argument broke out between them before she alleged that the husband and wife assaulted her.
"The couple also hurled abusive remarks at her and ordered her to leave the premises. Angered by their actions, the victim admitted that she retaliated by hurling insults at them," the source said.
The source said the woman subsequently lodged a police report following the incident.
She also claimed that her mobile phone had initially contained a video recording of the incident, but the footage was later found to have been deleted.
Dang Wangi acting police chief Superintendent Nuzulan, when contacted, confirmed that police received a report on the incident last night.
"The case is being investigated under Section 323 of the Penal Code for voluntarily causing hurt. Further investigations are underway to determine the actual cause of the incident," he said.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Cleaning supervisor charged with robbing, injuring four Rohingya men
Article:
JOHOR BARU: A cleaning company supervisor was charged at the Sessions and magistrate's courts here today with three counts of robbery and one count of injuring four Rohingya men in August and this month.
Muhammad Haziq Mohd Rizar, 26, pleaded not guilty to all charges read before judges N. Kanageswari and Datuk Che Wan Zaidi Che Wan Ibrahim, as well as magistrate A. Shaarmini.
For the first to third charges, the accused allegedly robbed three men who are United Nations High Commissioner for Refugees (UNHCR) cardholders.
He allegedly robbed the victims of a Honda C100 motorcycle key, a lawnmower, a set of motorcycle keys, a UNHCR card, and a tree branch cutter.
The offences were allegedly committed in Jalan Pekaka 3 and Jalan Pekaka 5, Taman Perling, here at 1.50pm and 2.30pm on Aug 26, and at a playground in Jalan Layang 12, Taman Perling, at 10am on Sept 9.
The charges were framed under Section 392 of the Penal Code, which carries a maximum jail term of 14 years, a fine, and whipping, upon conviction.
For the fourth charge, Muhammad Haziq allegedly voluntarily caused hurt to another Rohingya man near a playing field in Jalan Layang 3, Taman Perling, at 11.30am on Sept 9.
The charge was framed under Section 323 of the Penal Code, which provides for a jail term of up to one year, a fine of up to RM2,000, or both, upon conviction.
Deputy public prosecutors Nur Fatihah Mohd Nizam, Shamira Mohd Luthfi Ismail, and Anis Shafeeqah Shariffudin appeared for the prosecution, while lawyers Mohd Azlan Shah Mohd Allias and Jason Nazrin Tan represented the accused.
The courts granted total bail of RM16,000 for all four charges and fixed Oct 8 and Oct 28 for case mention.

Title: UN mission finds grounds to believe US committed war crimes in Iran
Article:
GENEVA: A UN fact-finding mission on Iran said on Thursday it had reasonable grounds to believe the United States was behind two military strikes on a school and sports facility in Iran in February, and that these constituted war crimes.
It also found that Iranian authorities committed crimes against humanity during their deadly crackdown on anti-government protests.
The findings in a new report by the Independent International Fact-Finding Mission on Iran, to be submitted to the UN Human Rights Council in Geneva, examined the US's conduct during the Iran war that began in February and the Iranian government's response to nationwide unrest that begun in late December.
The Iranian and US permanent missions in Geneva did not immediately respond to Reuters requests for comment.
US officials have previously said military operations are conducted in accordance with the law of armed conflict, while Iran has consistently rejected allegations of systematic rights violations.
The UN experts said they found reasonable grounds to believe US forces were responsible for an attack on the Shajareh Tayyebeh Primary School in the city of Minab, where more than 150 people were killed, including around 120 schoolchildren, according to Iranian officials.
The attack constituted an indiscriminate attack causing civilian deaths and damage to civilian infrastructure, amounting to a war crime under international law, the mission concluded.
According to the report, the US relied on intelligence suggesting a senior Iranian military commander was present at the site but failed to adequately verify the information before launching the strike. Investigators said the failure to update targeting intelligence and confirm the building was a military objective amounted to more than mere negligence.
"Rather, the US directed the strikes at the building of the school while being aware of a substantial risk of striking a civilian object and acting recklessly as regards the possibility that this would happen."
In June US President Donald Trump said that "nobody" purposefully attacked a girls' school in ​Iran in February, citing an investigation into the incident.
Reuters first ‌reported that an initial internal US military investigation showed US forces were likely responsible for the fatal strike in Minab in southern Iran.
The Pentagon has ​since elevated the probe but it has not published any ​preliminary findings.
UN experts said the school was a clearly identifiable civilian object and found no evidence that it was being used for military purposes.
The experts reached a similar conclusion over a strike on a sports centre in Lamerd.
The report said the attack damaged nearby residential buildings and a school and killed and injured 22 civilians.
It concluded that the strike was indiscriminate and therefore constituted a war crime.
US Central Command said in a statement in March that US forces did not launch any strikes into the city of Lamerd on that day.
The UN mission probe found that the Iranian authorities carried out a widespread and systematic attack against civilians during protests that erupted in late December last year, involving unlawful killings, torture, arbitrary detention, enforced disappearances and severe restrictions on freedom of expression.
Rights groups say bystanders were among those killed during the biggest crackdown since Shi'ite Muslim clerics took power in the 1979 revolution. Teheran blamed "terrorists and rioters" backed by exiled opponents and foreign foes the US and Israel.
The probe said it could not independently verify the death toll, but that it believed the number of dead and injured was likely far higher than official figures which say 3,038 people were killed, and 25,000 people injured.
The government's response to the protests - including violence and killings, cutting off the internet and use of the death penalty, marked a significant escalation from previous patterns of suppressing dissent, the report said.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: New MyKad pitched as fix for subsidy leakages
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: The new MyKad could help address long-standing problems in Malaysia's subsidy system by enabling beneficiaries to be verified in real time, according to its developr NexG Bhd.
The technology group said the new identity card combines biometric QR verification with an optional digital eWallet, allowing identity, authentication and payments to be linked through a single credential.
The system is designed to reduce duplication and leakages in subsidy distribution by allowing eligibility to be checked against verified identity information.
However, its wider use across government agencies and the private sector will depend on the necessary approvals and technical integration.
The new MyKad, produced and delivered by NexG's wholly-owned subsidiary Datasonic Technologies Sdn Bhd, will be carried by more than 24 million Malaysians, the company said in a statement today.
NexG said the biometric QR feature allows a live facial image to be matched against biometric records to verify that the person presenting the card is its genuine holder.
Currently, the National Registration Department (NRD) is the only government agency authorised to scan the QR code and conduct the biometric verification, NexG added.
Subject to approvals and inter-agency arrangements, the capability could subsequently be extended to other government agencies.
For commercial use, approved banks, telecommunications companies and merchants could use the system for customer onboarding, know-your-customer (KYC) and compliance checks without having to develop their own verification infrastructure.
The company said the MyKad's biometric QR capability could also complement MyDigital ID by providing an additional layer of identity verification, subject to technical integration and approvals.
NexG said the eWallet component is being provided to the government at no cost, while its use by citizens is optional.
It said the new MyKad could support digital transactions and public services while retaining the card's role as the country's sovereign identity credential.
The development comes as the government seeks to expand the digital economy, with a target for it to account for 30 per cent of gross domestic product by 2030.
NexG said its partnership with the government began with a MyKad-related contract in 1999 and has continued through successive generations of the national identity card.
Executive chairman Datuk Ishak Ismail said the company had served as a partner in safeguarding Malaysians' identities for 27 years.
The new MyKad represents the latest expansion of that role, from physical identification towards digital identity verification and transactions, he added.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Tuan Ibrahim: Public interest warrants continued push on Tabung Haji RCI findings
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Pas will continue to raise issues concerning the Royal Commission of Inquiry (RCI) report on Lembaga Tabung Haji (TH), including during next month's Dewan Rakyat sitting.
Pas deputy president Datuk Seri Tuan Ibrahim Tuan Man claimed that the delay in releasing the report had negative implications for the government, particularly as it was disclosed during the campaign for the Negri Sembilan election in July.
"The TH RCI issue will continue to be raised. The TH RCI investigation is of public interest, and it needs to be brought up based on all findings from the inquiry," he said when contacted today.
Speaking as a guest on the Sembang OhhYeahh! podcast broadcast yesterday, Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim said TH itself had requested the government to postpone disclosing the RCI findings when they were completed in 2022.
Anwar had said the
TH management made the request
out of concern that it could trigger mass withdrawals by depositors, affecting its operations.
The prime minister also raised the matter of Pas members of parliament walking out of the Dewan Rakyat and refusing to participate in debates when the RCI report was tabled on Aug 11.
Tuan Ibrahim, who is also Perikatan Nasional deputy chairman, said the party understood the implications of the disclosure on TH depositors, such as concerns over mass withdrawals.
"However, that is no excuse to delay presenting the report if explanations had been provided earlier," he said.
The RCI report was published on July 29, revealing key findings on the institution's management and governance between 2014 and 2020.
Several parties, including leaders from Umno and Perikatan Nasional, had questioned why the report was released during the Negri Sembilan election campaign.
During the Special Parliamentary Sitting to discuss the TH RCI report on Aug 11, opposition MPs from Pas and Wawasan walked out of the lower house after their motion to postpone the session was rejected by Dewan Rakyat Speaker Tan Sri Johari Abdul.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Lorry attendant gets one-year jail for spying on bathing stepdaughter, 12
Article:
BATU PAHAT: A lorry attendant who spied on his 12-year-old stepdaughter while she was bathing was sentenced to a year's jail today.
Magistrate Mustakim Sukarno sentenced the 26-year-old after he pleaded guilty to a charge under Section 509 of the Penal Code for a gesture intended to insult the modesty of a person.
Under the section, the accused could have been sentenced to up to five years in jail, a fine or both.
"The court took into account the relationship between the accused and the victim before handing down the sentence of a year's jail, taking effect from the date of arrest (Sept 10)," said Mustakim.
The father of three was accused of outraging the victim's modesty by spying on her while she bathed at a house in the district about 6.40am on Sept 9.
The girl's mother had lodged a report claiming that she had caught the accused spying on her bathing child through a gap in the pipe hole.
She said she had confronted the accused after that, adding that a similar incident had occurred in July.
The accused was arrested at 5.47pm the next day.
Prosecution was handled by deputy public prosecutor Nur Shahzleen Ibrahim, while the accused was represented to National Legal Aid Foundation lawyer Heng Eng Gee.

Title: Ketamine-positive woman arrested after swinging a knife at police
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: A woman in her 20s, who tested positive for ketamine, was arrested after allegedly swinging a knife at police officers during an attempted arrest in Jalan Chan Sow Lin here on Tuesday.
Cheras police chief Assistant Commissioner Mohd Rosdi Daud said police attempted to arrest the woman at 3.45pm.
"During the arrest, the suspect acted aggressively by grabbing a knife and attacking police officers," he said in a statement today.
He said checks found that the suspect had no previous criminal record.
Rosdi said preliminary urine screening showed that the suspect tested positive for ketamine.
"The suspect was remanded for four days to facilitate investigations under Section 324 of the Penal Code for voluntarily causing hurt by dangerous weapons or means, and Section 186 of the same law for obstructing a public servant," he said.

Title: Prosecution gets stay on hearing additional evidence in Rosmah's solar trial
Article:
PUTRAJAYA: The Court of Appeal today allowed the prosecution's application to stay the hearing of additional evidence from a key prosecution witness in Datin Seri Rosmah Mansor's RM1.25 billion Sarawak solar hybrid project corruption case.
A three-member panel led by Datuk Azhahari Kamal Ramli granted the application after deputy public prosecutor Mohd Asnawi Abu Hanipah informed the court that Rosmah did not object to the stay request.
"With the consent of both parties, we allow the application to stay the Court of Appeal's order dated Sept 1 until the prosecution's appeal is disposed of by the Federal Court.
"We hope the parties will inform the High Court of the Federal Court's decision as soon as it is delivered to facilitate case management at the High Court.
"The court has fixed Oct 7 for case management via e-Review and vacated the hearing for the main appeal originally scheduled for this October," said Azhahari, who sat with judges Datuk Dr Choo Kah Sing and K. Muniandy.
On Sept 1, the Court of Appeal allowed Rosmah's application to adduce additional evidence in her appeal against her conviction and sentence.
The panel subsequently ordered that the additional evidence involving the 16th prosecution witness, businessman Rayyan Radzwill Abdullah, be heard before a High Court judge.
Earlier, Asnawi said today's proceedings were initially fixed to hear the application to stay execution of the High Court order.
"However, this morning, the parties held discussions, and we were informed that the respondent does not object to the application to stay execution of the previous court order until the prosecution's appeal at the Federal Court is heard and decided.
"For the court's information, we filed a notice of appeal on Sept 4," said Asnawi, who appeared with DPPs Datuk Ahmad Akram Gharib and Mohamad Mustaffa P Kunyalam.
Lawyer Datuk Amer Hamzah Arshad, representing Rosmah, confirmed that the defence had no objection.
"I confirm that there have been serious discussions regarding this application. Given that the new evidence involves a key witness in the case and the prosecution itself has given an assurance that it will expedite appeal proceedings at the Federal Court, we have no objection.
"In the interest of both parties, it is appropriate for the appeal at the Federal Court to be heard and decided first," he said, adding that parties would attend High Court proceedings this afternoon to update the court on the status.
Rosmah, 74, had applied to adduce additional evidence comprising a police report and a statutory declaration affirmed by Rayyan Radzwill.
In the statutory declaration, Rayyan Radzwill alleged that he was pressured by the prosecution during trial and presented documentary material challenging the credibility of his testimony.
On Sept 1, 2022, the High Court convicted Rosmah on three corruption charges under Section 16(a)(A) of the Malaysian Anti-Corruption Commission (MACC) Act 2009.
She was found guilty of soliciting RM187.5 million and receiving RM6.5 million from former Jepak Holdings managing director Saidi Abang Samsudin through her former aide, Datuk Rizal Mansor.
The gratification was an inducement to assist Jepak Holdings in securing a RM1.25 billion hybrid solar project from the Education Ministry to supply electricity to 369 rural schools in Sarawak.
Rosmah was sentenced to 10 years' jail for each charge, to run concurrently, and fined RM970 million. She was granted a stay of execution pending appeal.
