Title: Buzze Azam fails to overturn RM15,000 fine over Facebook post
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Lawyer Mohd Khairul Azam Abdul Aziz, also known as Buzze Azam, has failed to overturn his conviction and RM15,000 fine over an offensive Facebook post criticising the criminal justice system.
High Court judge Datuk Aslam Zainuddin dismissed Khairul Azam's appeals against both his conviction and sentence, as well as the prosecution's appeal for a heavier sentence.
Khairul Azam had been charged under Section 233(1)(a) of the Communications and Multimedia Act 1998 over a Facebook post published on March 24, 2021.
The post was subsequently read at the Malaysian Communications and Multimedia Commission office in Wangsa Maju at about 3.50pm the following day.
In his grounds of decision dated today, Aslam said the post went beyond expressing dissatisfaction with the administration of criminal justice.
He said although it touched on issues capable of legitimate public discussion, including prosecutorial decisions and the burden imposed on accused persons pending trial, the language used was aggressive, abusive and calculated to outrage.
"The tone and wording of the post show that it was not merely an expression of opinion on systemic weaknesses, but a targeted communication intended to disparage the institutions and officeholders named or plainly implicated," he said.
The judge said the post was directed at identifiable institutions, namely the Attorney-General's Chambers and the police, although they were not expressly named in the charge.
He rejected Khairul Azam's argument that the charge was defective as it did not identify the person or body allegedly annoyed.
Aslam said the charge, when read together with its particulars and the evidence, sufficiently conveyed the essential ingredients of the offence and enabled Khairul Azam to know the case he had to meet.
The judge also rejected the argument that the Facebook post amounted to protected criticism under Article 10 of the Federal Constitution.
"There is a clear distinction between fair criticism, even if robust, and abusive speech directed at causing insult or annoyance.
"In the present case, the post was not framed as a reasoned critique of policy, procedure, or institutional performance.
"It was a crude and insulting attack in vulgar terms," he said.
Aslam said a person could strongly criticise public institutions while remaining within the bounds of lawful speech.
"Once the language becomes a deliberate vehicle for abuse, the protection of free expression is not engaged in the same way."
The court also rejected Khairul Azam's argument that a subsequent amendment to Section 233, which changed the threshold from "offensive" to "grossly offensive", should apply retrospectively to his case.
The judge also found no merit in Khairul Azam's contention that the RM15,000 fine was manifestly excessive.
He said sentencing was primarily a matter for the trial court and an appellate court would intervene only where a sentence was plainly wrong, excessive or inadequate.
Aslam also dismissed the prosecution's appeal seeking an enhanced sentence on grounds that the RM15,000 fine remained within the range reasonably open to the trial court.
He said the fact that another court might have imposed a different sentence was insufficient to justify appellate intervention.
Khairul Azam was represented by Awang Armadajaya Awang Mahmud and Nur Jehan Abu Bakar, while deputy public prosecutor Mohamad Fadhly Mohd Zamry appeared for the prosecution.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Malaysia's fiscal deficit seen narrowing in 2027: JP Morgan
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Malaysia's fiscal deficit is expected to narrow to 3.4 per cent of gross domestic product (GDP) in 2027, from a projected 3.5 per cent this year, according to JP Morgan.
The US investment bank said the government was balancing near-term support measures with increasingly binding medium-term fiscal constraints.
These include higher oil prices, rising debt-servicing costs and an elevated starting level of public debt, which could limit fiscal room for further spending.
JP Morgan said the government has progressively reduced the deficit from 6.4 per cent of GDP in 2021 to 3.7 per cent in 2025 via a mix of revenue enhancing and expenditure reducing measures.
"Against the more challenging backdrop, we expect fiscal consolidation to continue, albeit at a slower pace, with 2027 Budget likely to prioritise a reallocation rather than an expansion of overall spending," it said.
The firm expects the budget to reprioritise rather than significantly expand overall spending, with some savings likely to come from a lower projected subsidy bill in 2027 due to lower projected oil prices.
JP Morgan forecasted for the oil prices to hit US$85 per barrel this year and US$63 in 2027.
"In this regard, the government's pre-budget statement indicates that 2027 Budget will focus on alleviating cost-of-living pressures, including through the existing cash transfer and subsidy frameworks, while also maintaining fiscal discipline.
"This could imply a further moderation in development expenditure from the 3.7 per cent of GDP projected for 2026, as revenues are channelled towards household support measures and debt servicing costs," it said.
The firm also said that fiscal pressures have eased since April, but not gone away entirely.
The government had initially budgeted RM15 billion for fuel subsidies in 2026 but now expects total fuel subsidy outlays to reach RM40 billion, implying a RM25 billion increase, down from the RM43 billion increase projected in April.
It said part of this excess subsidy bill should be offset by stronger-than-budgeted revenues, including higher petroleum-related tax receipts and royalties.
"Stronger nominal GDP growth should also help compress the deficit ratio through a larger denominator effect.
"Under our central scenario of eight and nine per cent nominal GDP growth this year, the fiscal deficit could still meet the government's 3.5 per cent of GDP target even with a modest RM2 billion-3 billion overshoot in the nominal deficit.
"Even so, we expect some residual shortfall to remain, necessitating additional revenue-mobilising measures, such as a special dividend from Petroliam Nasional Bhd, to achieve the fiscal target," it said.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Kepong restaurant assault: Technician seeks lesser charge through A-GC representation
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: A technician charged with causing grievous hurt to a businessman during a restaurant attack has submitted a representation to the Attorney-General's Chambers (A-GC), seeking a reduction of the charge against him.
Lawyer Muhamad Firdaus Jumaludin, who represents Lai Kae Bin, 33, said the representation was submitted on Sept 2 for a review of the charge under Section 326 of the Penal Code.
Firdaus said Lai had instructed him to seek a lesser charge, as he felt the existing charge was too serious.
"We went through the evidence and did not see any intention on his part to commit the act. It happened in the spur of the moment," he said after proceedings before Sessions Court judge Noor Aini Yusof today.
Lai is one of
three men
charged with voluntarily causing grievous hurt to businessman Andrew Teh, 47, using dangerous weapons at Restoran Hing Kee Bakuteh in Jalan Kepong at 2am on May 7.
The other two accused are carpenter Wong Weng Luen, 49, and memorial centre worker Wan Ken Fei, 30.
All three have pleaded not guilty to the charge.
Only Lai and Wan were present in the dock during today's proceedings, while several of their family members sat in the public gallery.
Wong was not brought to court as he is currently undergoing psychiatric assessment at Hospital Bahagia Ulu Kinta in Perak, following a court order last month.
Deputy public prosecutor Adiba Iman Hassan said the prosecution had yet to receive Wong's psychiatric report as the hospital required another month to complete the assessment.
She also confirmed that the A-GC had received Lai's representation, which was still under review.
"Besides the psychiatric report, we have yet to receive the closed-circuit television (CCTV) forensic report and the victim's full medical reports from private and government hospitals.
"I also wish to record that the prosecution has handed over documents to Lai's lawyer," she said.
Noor Aini ordered Wong to remain at the hospital for assessment and fixed Oct 13 for mention of the psychiatric report.
The same date was set for the prosecution to hand over additional documents.
Lawyer Mohammad Arifin Abdul Wahab appeared on behalf of lawyer S. Narasimham, who represents Wan.
Meanwhile, lawyer Keith Moo, who held a watching brief for Teh, said the victim had yet to fully recover and was still receiving hospital treatment.
The attack allegedly stemmed from an incident in which Teh was accused of staring at a man believed to be intoxicated while dining at the restaurant.
Closed-circuit television footage of the several-minute assault later went viral on social media.
The footage showed Teh seated at a table before one of the men approached and began attacking him.
Two others then joined in, initially appearing to restrain their friend before taking part in the assault.
Teh was punched, kicked and struck with various objects, including chairs and a kettle, before managing to escape.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Zulkifli: People of faith should not mock or insult other religions
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Jokes that mock, insult, ridicule and demean others are strictly prohibited by and contradicts the teachings of Islam.
Minister in the Prime Minister's Department (Religious Affairs) Senator Dr Zulkifli Hasan said Verse 11 of Surah Al-Hujurat clearly forbids believers from insulting fellow human beings, mocking, calling each other by bad nicknames, and denouncing one another.
"In every speech or address, a leader should elevate mature discourse, focusing on national development and the strengthening of unity, rather than being tainted by sexually suggestive jokes, let alone those that touch upon the sensitivities of other religious institutions.
"The act of turning symbols or figures of any religion into the butt of jokes degrades the values of leadership etiquette and tears apart the inter-religious harmony that has always been upheld in this country," he said in a statement.
Zulkifli said, as leaders who serve as role models for society, particularly those who are Muslims, such lapses in judgment should be realised and addressed properly.
"I urge all parties to refocus on issues concerning the people's interests and cultivate a public discourse based on wisdom, politeness, and high moral values," he said.
He was commenting on the controversy surrounding the speech by Sepang Umno Division chief Datuk Noorazli Said at the party's recent general assembly in which he made a suggestive joke about a priest and a nun.
Noorazli's joke angered many people, with one minister calling for him to
be investigated
.
Several people also questioned the sincerity of his apology, but Noorazli
defended it
, saying only God would know what was in a person's heart.
Meanwhile, when met after a function at World Trade Centre Kuala Lumpur, Zulkifli said anything which went against religious values should be rejected.
He reiterated that no one should joke about anything which touched on religious sensitivities, adding that this was in line with the views of Islamic scholars.
"What we need to do is focus our discourse on matters that strengthen the soul and unity, that bring people together. Malaysians should stay away from anything that goes against these values," he said.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Gas Malaysia teams up with France's Air Liquide on low-carbon energy
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Gas Malaysia Bhd has teamed up with France's Air Liquide Engineering & Construction to explore opportunities in low-carbon hydrogen, carbon dioxide off-take and bio-liquefied natural gas in Malaysia.
The two companies will assess potential projects combining Gas Malaysia's market reach and gas infrastructure with Air Liquide's expertise in industrial gas technologies and engineering.
The memorandum of understanding was signed on the sidelines of Gastech 2026 in Bangkok, Gas Malaysia said in a statement.
"The companies will also leverage Air Liquide's technology for low-carbon hydrogen solutions. In addition, both parties will assess wider prospects that enable industrial decarbonisation and a lower-carbon economy through advanced engineering and technological solutions," it said.
Gas Malaysia president and group chief executive officer Azli Mohamed said the collaboration was part of the company's efforts to expand beyond conventional gas supply into renewable gas, hydrogen and other lower-carbon industrial solutions.
"Through this collaborative framework, the two companies will explore opportunities that combine Gas Malaysia's market reach and gas infrastructure network with Air Liquide's global capabilities in technology and engineering to help customers navigate the energy transition," he said.
Gas Malaysia said the collaboration was aligned with its GM32 strategy and ongoing decarbonisation initiatives, as well as Malaysia's National Energy Transition Roadmap, particularly its push for lower-carbon energy alternatives and industrial decarbonisation.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Zahid arrives in Jakarta for 4-day working visit
Article:
JAKARTA: Deputy Prime Minister Datuk Seri Dr Ahmad Zahid Hamidi arrived here for a working visit aimed at strengthening Malaysia-Indonesia cooperation in disaster management, including forest and land fires, as well as the halal industry and rural development.
Zahid arrived at Halim Perdanakusuma International Airport here at 1.15pm local time and was welcomed by Malaysian Ambassador-designate to Indonesia Datuk Muzaffar Shah Mustafa, head of Indonesia's Halal Product Assurance Organising Agency (BPJPH) Ahmad Haikal Hasan and Indonesian officials.
Zahid is scheduled to hold a meeting with Indonesian Vice-President Gibran Rakabuming Raka at the Vice-Presidential Palace.
Gibran is expected to be accompanied by Home Affairs Minister Muhammad Tito Karnavian, Marine Affairs and Fisheries Minister Sakti Wahyu Trenggono, Villages and Development of Disadvantaged Regions Minister Yandri Susanto and Environment Minister Mohamad Jumhur Hidayat.
Zahid, who is also rural and regional development minister, is scheduled to proceed to the Villages and Development of Disadvantaged Regions Ministry later today, where the two ministers are set to sign a memorandum of understanding to strengthen cooperation in rural development.
The four-day visit, which ends on Sunday (Sept 20), is at the invitation of BPJPH in conjunction with the fifth Halal 20 (H20) Summit.
Zahid is scheduled to attend the summit's opening ceremony tomorrow and participate as a panellist in a session on regional halal cooperation.
Malaysia-Indonesia bilateral trade reached US$24.22 billion (US$1=RM4.08) in 2025, while Malaysia remained Indonesia's fourth-largest investor, with investments amounting to US$4.5 billion.
People-to-people ties also remained strong, with more than 2.63 million Malaysians visiting Indonesia last year, making Malaysia the republic's largest source of foreign tourists, while 4.26 million Indonesians visited Malaysia.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Indonesia to begin e-commerce tax collection from Oct 1, media reports
Article:
JAKARTA: Indonesia will begin making e-commerce platforms collect income taxes from sellers starting Oct 1, a month earlier than previously announced, local media reported on Thursday, citing the tax chief.
The move reverses a delay ordered by the previous finance minister and follows a shake-up at the top of the finance ministry this week.
The finance ministry and the tax office did not immediately respond to a Reuters request for comment.
Some of the biggest platforms operating in Southeast Asia's largest economy were originally tasked by the tax office to start collecting taxes from sellers beginning in August, but then-finance minister Purbaya Yudhi Sadewa ordered a delay on Aug 5 because of concern it might hurt purchasing power.
The next day, the tax office said the policy would be delayed to Nov 1 and promised taxes that were already paid would be refunded.
Purbaya was sacked this week and his deputy, veteran technocrat Suahasil Nazara, was named as President Prabowo Subianto's third finance minister in less than two years.
"God willing, we will immediately activate the regulation and implementation. They are ready, we are ready," the head of the finance ministry's tax department, Bimo Wijayanto, said, according to CNBC Indonesia, adding the collection will begin Oct 1. "There's no drama."
Sources told Reuters Purbaya had clashed with top officials in his ministry prior to his removal, including with Bimo, over the reshuffling of hundreds of officials at the ministry.
​Tokopedia, controlled by ByteDance's TikTok and ​partly owned by Indonesia's biggest tech company GoTo, together with Sea Limited's Shopee, the Alibaba-backed Lazada, and Blibli, had previously been appointed as tax collectors.
Indonesia has a booming e-commerce industry, with an estimated gross merchandise value of US$71 billion in 2025 that is expected to grow to US$140 billion by 2030, according to a report by Google, Singapore state investor Temasek and consultancy Bain & Co.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Vodus study puts Anwar ahead of PM hopefuls with highest acceptance and first-choice support
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 17 — Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim has emerged as the strongest overall candidate for the prime ministership in a new national study by Vodus Research, recording the highest public acceptance, first-choice support and net acceptance among five prominent prospective candidates.
The Malaysia Prime Minister Candidate Study 2026 found that 46 per cent of respondents aware of the candidates said they would accept Anwar as prime minister, while 34 per cent named him as their first choice.
His net acceptance score stood at +19 percentage points, also the highest among the five candidates surveyed.
Anwar was also the most widely recognised figure in the study, with 93 per cent familiarity among respondents aware of the candidates.
His support was particularly strong in East Malaysia, where 41 per cent of respondents selected him as their top choice, compared with 28 per cent in Peninsular Malaysia.
Vodus Research founder Kelvin Goh said the findings showed that public assessments of potential national leaders went beyond a simple popularity contest, with familiarity, favourability, acceptability and first-choice support representing distinct measures.
“Anwar’s stronger support in East Malaysia may partly reflect his administration’s greater focus on Sabah and Sarawak, including progress on MA63-related matters, Sabah’s revenue entitlements, and Sarawak’s greater control over its resources,” he said in a statement.
“These moves have kept federal delivery, state rights, and fiscal fairness highly visible in the region, which may have strengthened perceptions of Anwar’s leadership there.”
Khairy Jamaluddin recorded 32 per cent acceptance and a net acceptance score of +15 percentage points, while Johor Menteri Besar Datuk Onn Hafiz Ghazi registered 17 per cent acceptance and +6 points.
Terengganu Menteri Besar Datuk Seri Ahmad Samsuri Mokhtar recorded 13 per cent acceptance, while Datuk Seri Rafizi Ramli had 17 per cent acceptance and a net acceptance score of -3 points.
The study also found that Anwar’s first-choice support was more than twice that of Khairy, who recorded 14 per cent, while Onn Hafiz and Rafizi each registered eight per cent and Samsuri six per cent.
On personal favourability, however, Khairy recorded the highest net favourability score at +51 points, followed by Samsuri at +44, Onn Hafiz at +43, Anwar at +39 and Rafizi at +32.
Among those who viewed Anwar favourably, respondents most often cited his ability to grow the economy and create opportunities, as well as his experience in leading Malaysia, handling foreign affairs, attracting foreign investment and governance.
Across the study, economic growth and opportunities, a clear vision for Malaysia, strong and capable leadership, and improving Malaysians’ living standards were among the recurring factors respondents associated with favourable views of political figures.
The study involved 1,482 Malaysian adults aged 18 and above nationwide, with fieldwork conducted from Aug 18 to Sept 1.
Vodus said the findings represented a snapshot of public views during the fieldwork period and were not an electoral forecast or endorsement of any candidate or political party.

Title: Army steps up drone surveillance on border routes amid unrest in southern Thailand
Article:
MELAKA, Sept 17 — The Malaysian Army (TDM) is using advanced drone technology to strengthen security monitoring in hard-to-reach areas along the Malaysia-Thailand border, particularly in response to the unrest in southern Thailand.
Chief of Army Gen Tan Sri Azhan Md Othman said the technology enabled TDM to overcome the challenges posed by hilly and densely forested terrain, where physical patrols by troops were difficult.
“It is true that the border stretches over a long distance, and there are areas that cannot be patrolled due to the terrain.
“So, the aerial assets are used to gather information and provide a real-time overview before ground units are deployed to take further action,” he told Bernama at Terendak Camp, Sungai Udang here today.
Azhan also gave an assurance that border security remained tight, with round-the-clock operations in place.
“We do not deny that the terrain provides opportunities for illegal routes, but the situation remains under control. We will ensure that no elements are able to breach our border. There will be no compromise.
“Our personnel are provided with clear rules of engagement, under which firm and decisive action will be taken immediately,” he added.
Meanwhile, Azhan said his recent official visit to Russia, at the invitation of the Russian Ground Forces, was aimed at strengthening bilateral military ties.
“The main areas discussed with our Russian counterparts included training cooperation and opportunities for course exchanges, particularly in combined arms and artillery.
“Both sides are now in the final stages of finalising the arrangements before TDM personnel are sent to undergo the specialised training,” he said. — Bernama

Title: KLIA ranks first in Asia for connectivity in OAG Megahubs 2026 ranking
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 17 — Kuala Lumpur International Airport (KUL) ranked fourth globally and first among all Asian airports in OAG’s Megahubs 2026 ranking, with connections to 154 destinations, while also topping the Low-Cost Carrier (LCC) Megahubs index with nearly 15,000 possible low-cost connections.
OAG, the intelligence partner for global travel, said its annual ranking of global airport connectivity showed Asia Pacific (APAC) dominating the index, with eight airports in the global top 20.
According to OAG in a statement, AirAsia operates 34 per cent of total flights at KUL, while Seoul Incheon ranked second in the LCC rankings with connectivity reaching 198 destinations.
The recovery of Chinese airports was another standout feature in APAC, with Shanghai Pudong rising from 19th to 14th globally, Guangzhou Baiyun International from 36th to 19th, and Hong Kong returning to the global top 20 at 20th. Tokyo Haneda also improved, rising from ninth to eighth globally.
“The Asia Pacific numbers tell two stories this year. The first is the completion of Chinese aviation's post-pandemic recovery; these airports are back in the top 20, and the data shows it.
“The second is how low-cost carriers have reshaped Southeast Asian connectivity, with 51 per cent of all seats in the region now operated by LCCs, well above the global average,” said OAG Head of APAC, Mayur Patel.
OAG added that Singapore Changi climbed significantly in the LCC rankings, from 10th to fifth, reflecting growth in destinations served and potential low-cost connections, while Fukuoka rose from 13th to eighth in the LCC index.
The average dominant carrier share at APAC’s top 10 airports is 33 per cent, lower than in most other regions, reflecting the diverse mix of full-service and low-cost carriers serving different traveller segments across Southeast and Northeast Asia. — Bernama

Title: Kota Kinabalu airport runway temporarily closed for rectification works
Article:
KOTA KINABALU, Sept 17 — The runway at Kota Kinabalu International Airport has been temporarily closed to facilitate rectification works, Malaysia Airports Holdings Bhd (MAHB) said today.
In a notice on Facebook, MAHB said a Notice to Airmen (NOTAM) had been issued over the temporary closure.
“The runway will reopen once the necessary safety inspections and clearing works have been completed,” it said.
Passengers have been advised to check with their respective airlines for the latest flight status and updates.
MAHB did not provide details on the nature of the rectification works or how long the runway would remain closed.

Title: Papagomo fails to stay RM280,000 defamation payout to Lim Guan Eng, son
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 17 — The High Court today dismissed an application by Wan Muhammad Azri Wan Deris, better known as Papagomo, to stay the execution of a judgment ordering him to pay RM280,000 in damages to former Penang Chief Minister Lim Guan Eng and his son.
Judge Roslan Mat Nor, in dismissing the application, ruled that the defendant had failed to establish any special circumstances warranting a stay of execution pending the disposal of his appeal, which was filed on June 2.
“The defendant claimed that he would succeed in his appeal and that the appeal would be rendered academic if the judgment sum was paid now. The defendant also contended that he would face bankruptcy proceedings if the plaintiffs executed the judgment.
“These reasons do not assist the court in exercising its discretion to grant a stay,” he said, and ordered Wan Muhammad Azri to pay RM5,000 in costs.
On May 19 this year, the court ruled that Wan Muhammad Azri was liable for defamation and ordered him to pay RM280,000 in damages to Guan Eng and Clint Lim Way Chau over the latter's posts alleging that Way Chau was detained in Singapore for purportedly bringing in RM2 million in undeclared cash in 2020.
The court ordered the defendant to pay global damages of RM200,000 and costs of RM30,000 to Guan Eng as well as damages of RM80,000 and costs of RM10,000 to the second plaintiff (Way Chau).
The duo filed the suit on April 19, 2020, alleging that the defendant had posted defamatory statements on his Facebook page claiming that Way Chau was detained at Changi Airport on February 29, 2020, for bringing in RM2 million in undeclared cash.
Guan Eng said the defendant, who uploaded the post under the name ‘Papa Azri’ on March 14, 2020, also claimed that Guan Eng had travelled to Singapore on February 29, 2020, after the alleged detention.
Lawyer Simon Murali attended today's proceedings, representing both plaintiffs, while lawyer Fazilah Jaafar represented Wan Muhammad Azri. — Bernama

Title: Palm oil mill shut down after pump failure sends effluent into Johor’s Sungai Sembrong
Article:
KLUANG, Sept 17 — A palm oil mill in Kluang has been identified as the source of pollution in Sungai Sembrong and ordered to halt operations immediately.
The directive was issued by the Kluang branch of the Department of Environment (DoE) following an investigation and inspection of the facility after pollution in the river was first detected on Monday.
“Further investigation revealed a pump malfunction at the mill’s effluent treatment pond, causing an overflow of oil-contaminated effluent into Sungai Sembrong.
“The mill has been ordered to halt operations immediately and is required to carry out cleanup and repair works. Follow-up action on the suspension of its licence is also underway,” the DoE said in a statement today.
Dead fish and prawns had previously been found along stretches of Sungai Sembrong, with the pollution reportedly affecting the livelihoods of nearby Orang Asli villagers.
The DoE reminded industries, particularly palm oil mill operators, to strictly comply with requirements under the Environmental Quality Act 1974 and the department’s licensing conditions.
It warned that stern action, including the suspension or revocation of licences, would be taken against any breach of the Act that causes environmental pollution or threatens drinking water supplies or public health.

Title: BPHB unit appointed Bintulu Port operator for 30 years
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 17 — Bintulu Port Authority (Sarawak) has appointed Bintulu Port Holdings Bhd's (BPHB) wholly-owned subsidiary Bintulu Port Sdn Bhd (BPSB) as an approved port operator for Bintulu Port for 30 years, from September 1, 2026 to August 31, 2056.
BPHB said the appointment was approved by the Sarawak legislative assembly.
“The appointment is set out in the Bintulu Port Authority (Sarawak) (Appointment of Approved Port Operator) Notification, 2026, published in the Sarawak Government Gazette, Part II, dated September 10, 2026. The notification was made under section 12(2)(a) of the Port Authorities Ordinance, 1961,” it said in a stock exchange filing.
On June 23, 2026, the Sarawak Ministry of Infrastructure and Port Development notified BPSB that the government had approved in principle the appointment of BPSB as the approved port operator for Bintulu Port under Section 12(2)(a) of the Port Authorities Ordinance, 1961.
BPHB said BPSB “shall perform, carry out or provide the port undertakings at Bintulu Port subject to full compliance with the ordinance and any by-laws, regulations or subsidiary legislation made under it.”
BPSB will also carry out the terms and conditions of the Heads of Agreement (HOA) dated July 27, 2026, entered into between the Sarawak state government, Bintulu Port Authority and BPSB, it added.
“The HOA terms and conditions shall continue to apply until the Port Operation Concession Agreement (POCA) is duly executed by those parties. Upon execution, the POCA shall be binding on BPSB and govern its operation of Bintulu Port,” said BPHB. — Bernama

Title: PMO says letter claiming Cabinet approval for PLUS highway widening is fake
Article:
PUTRAJAYA, Sept 17 — The Prime Minister’s Office (PMO) today said that a letter dated July 17, 2026, claiming that Cabinet approval had been given for a proposed Private Finance Initiative (PFI) project to widen the North-South Expressway (PLUS) is fake.
In a statement today, PMO stressed that the Prime Minister had never issued or signed the letter and denied any connection with the document or the purported approval.
“PMO has lodged a police report over the forgery of the document and the misuse of the Prime Minister’s name and PMO’s official identity.
“Appropriate legal action will be taken against any party found to be involved,” the statement read.
PMO therefore advised the public not to be deceived by, circulate, or share the fake document. — Bernama

Title: Critics of Anwar should back their words with action, says PKR Youth chief
Article:
IPOH, Sept 17 — PKR Youth chief Muhammad Kamil Abdul Munim has hit out at those criticising Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim, saying some were quick to make political statements but lacked the courage to follow through with their actions.
He said while there were political statements suggesting that the country was currently unstable, the government remained committed to ensuring political stability as a foundation for economic stability and, ultimately, the benefit of the people.
“Our priority is to ensure political stability because from there, we can ensure economic stability, which will ultimately benefit the people,” he said.
He spoke to reporters after presenting allocations to non-governmental organisations in the Prime Minister’s Tambun parliamentary constituency at the Penghulu Mukim Hulu Kinta Office here.
Muhammad Kamil, who is also Anwar’s political secretary, said he did not deny that certain groups were deliberately attempting to create political instability to serve the interests and demands of certain leaders within their respective parties.
“Today, what we can assure the people is that the current government, particularly the Prime Minister, is committed to ensuring that all policies and plans can be implemented and that the government works for the good and benefit of the people as a whole,” he said.
He said this remained the case despite some statements appearing to attack Anwar personally.
“Some people are brave enough to talk, but they are not brave enough to act.
“So, we need to assess which leaders are working and which leaders are merely playing politics. I think the people can make a good assessment of that,” he said.
Muhammad Kamil also said there appeared to be confusion among the public when some political figures called for the 16th general election (GE16) to be held soon while at the same time saying they would remain in the government until the end of its term.
“That is something you have to ask that person. In the morning they say one thing, and at night they say another. They are confusing people,” he said.
Muhammad Kamil was responding to recent remarks made during the Umno general assembly, where party president Datuk Seri Ahmad Zahid Hamidi challenged Anwar to remove Umno from the unity government and face a confidence vote in Parliament.
Ahmad Zahid was also reported to have reminded coalition partners that Anwar’s administration remained in power with Umno’s support.
“The Prime Minister is the prime minister because of Umno’s support,” Ahmad Zahid was quoted as saying.
Ahmad Zahid was also reported to have backed calls for an earlier general election during the assembly.

Title: Melaka assembly dissolution date still undecided, says CM
Article:
ALOR GAJAH, Sept 17 — The date for the dissolution of the Melaka State Legislative Assembly to pave the way for the state election has yet to be set, said Chief Minister Datuk Seri Ab Rauf Yusoh.
Ab Rauf, who is also Melaka Barisan Nasional (BN) chairman, said several state administrative matters needed to be resolved first to ensure all plans proceeded smoothly before the assembly was dissolved.
“I am giving an indication that the Melaka State Assembly will be dissolved from Friday to Friday because within that period, we still have many matters that need to be resolved to govern the state,” he told reporters here today.
He was speaking after officiating the 2026 Melaka State-level Senior Citizens Day, Persons with Disabilities (PwD) Day and Children's Day celebration in conjunction with the Tanjung Bidara constituency's
Wakil Rakyat Untuk Rakyat
(WRUR) programme here.
Ab Rauf said the date would be announced to the media and the public once it had been finalised.
On Tuesday, allegations went viral on WhatsApp claiming that Melaka Yang Dipertua Negeri Tun Mohd Ali Rustam had signed the Melaka State Assembly dissolution document together with Ab Rauf during a meeting at the Guest Room of the Chief Executive Officer's Office at the Melaka International Trade Centre (MITC) in Ayer Keroh.
The Melaka State Assembly has 28 seats, while the current state government's mandate expires on December 31. — Bernama

Title: Court of Appeal stays Rosmah’s additional evidence hearing pending Federal Court appeal
Article:
PUTRAJAYA, Sept 17 — The Court of Appeal today allowed the prosecution’s application to stay the hearing of additional evidence from a key prosecution witness in Datin Seri Rosmah Mansor’s corruption case involving the RM1.25 billion Sarawak solar hybrid project.
A three-member panel led by Datuk Azhahari Kamal Ramli granted the application after Deputy Public Prosecutor (DPP) Mohd Asnawi Abu Hanipah informed the court that Rosmah did not object to the request.
“With the consent of both parties, we allow the application to stay the Court of Appeal’s order dated September 1 until the prosecution’s appeal is disposed of by the Federal Court.
“We hope the parties will inform the High Court of the Federal Court’s decision as soon as it is delivered to facilitate case management at the High Court.
“The court has fixed October 7 for case management via e-Review and vacated the hearing for the main appeal originally scheduled for this October,” said Azhahari, who sat with Judges Datuk Dr Choo Kah Sing and K. Muniandy.
On September 1, the Court of Appeal allowed Rosmah’s application to adduce additional evidence in her appeal against her conviction and sentence.
The panel subsequently ordered that the additional evidence involving the 16th prosecution witness, businessman Rayyan Radzwill Abdullah, be heard before a High Court judge.
Earlier, Mohd Asnawi said today’s proceedings had initially been fixed for the hearing of the application to stay the execution of the High Court order.
“However, this morning, the parties held discussions, and we were informed that the respondent does not object to the application to stay the execution of the previous court order until the prosecution’s appeal at the Federal Court is heard and decided.
“For the court’s information, we filed a notice of appeal on September 4,” said Mohd Asnawi, who is handling the case with Deputy Public Prosecutors Datuk Ahmad Akram Gharib and Mohamad Mustaffa P Kunyalam.
Lawyer Datuk Amer Hamzah Arshad, representing Rosmah, confirmed that the defence did not object to the application.
“I confirm that there have been serious discussions regarding this application. Given that the new evidence involves a key witness in the case and the prosecution itself has given an assurance that it will expedite the appeal proceedings at the Federal Court, we have no objection.
“In the interest of both parties, it is appropriate for the appeal at the Federal Court to be heard and decided first,” he said, adding that the parties would attend the High Court proceedings this afternoon to update the court on the status of the appeal at the Court of Appeal.
Rosmah, 74, had applied to adduce additional evidence comprising a police report and a statutory declaration affirmed by businessman Rayyan Radzwill Abdullah.
In the statutory declaration, Rayyan Radzwill alleged, among other things, that he was pressured by the prosecution during the trial, and presented documentary material challenging the credibility of his testimony.
On September 1, 2022, the High Court convicted Rosmah of three corruption charges under Section 16(a)(A) of the Malaysian Anti-Corruption Commission (MACC) Act 2009.
She was found guilty of soliciting RM187.5 million and receiving RM6.5 million from former Jepak Holdings managing director Saidi Abang Samsudin through her former aide, Datuk Rizal Mansor.
The gratification was an inducement for Rosmah to assist Jepak Holdings in securing a RM1.25 billion hybrid solar project from the Ministry of Education to supply electricity to 369 rural schools in Sarawak.
Rosmah was sentenced to 10 years in prison for each charge, to run concurrently, and fined RM970 million. She was granted a stay of execution pending her appeal. — Bernama

Title: Negeri Sembilan MB instructs state secretary to gazette Tuanku Muhriz’s removal despite DKU objection
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 17 — Negri Sembilan Menteri Besar Datuk Ismail Lasim has instructed the state secretary to proceed with gazetting the removal of Tuanku Muhriz Tuanku Munawir as Yang di-Pertuan Besar, despite the Dewan Keadilan dan Undang (DKU) saying the state executive council has no jurisdiction to determine the ruler’s position.
According to
Free Malaysia Today
(FMT) Ismail told reporters after an event in Seremban that he endorsed the statement issued by the state executive council yesterday affirming Tuanku Muhriz’s removal.
He said the exco had unanimously agreed on the position when it met on Tuesday.
Ismail said the state secretary had been asked to proceed with gazetting the proclamation on Tuanku Muhriz’s removal “according to the relevant regulations”.
Ismail declined to take further questions from reporters, FMT reported.
The exco’s statement yesterday affirmed that Tuanku Muhriz’s removal in April was legitimate and that Tuanku Nadzaruddin Tuanku Ja’afar was the new ruler of Negeri Sembilan.
The development comes despite the DKU maintaining that the state executive council has no jurisdiction to determine the validity of the proclamation or the position of the Yang di-Pertuan Besar.
In a statement today, the DKU said the exco’s September 16 decision had no legal effect insofar as it purported to confirm Tuanku Muhriz’s removal, recognise a new ruler and order its immediate implementation.
The DKU maintained that Tuanku Muhriz remained the legitimate Yang di-Pertuan Besar and that questions involving Malay adat, including the appointment and removal of the ruler, fell within its jurisdiction under the Negri Sembilan Constitution.
It also said the matter was before the High Court in Seremban and urged all parties to respect the legal process.
Meanwhile, lawyers for Tuanku Muhriz accused the state government of staging a coup by declaring his removal, saying yesterday’s statement breached interim injunctions issued by the High Court on June 5.
They said they intended to commence contempt proceedings against the state government over the alleged breach of the injunctions.

Title: Quit if you no longer recognise Tuanku Muhriz as ruler, Loke tells Negeri Sembilan exco members
Article:
SEREMBAN, Sept 17 — DAP secretary-general Anthony Loke Siew Fook today called on Negeri Sembilan executive council members to resign if they no longer recognise Tuanku Muhriz Tuanku Munawir as the state’s Yang di-Pertuan Besar.
The Seremban MP questioned whether the Exco had the legal authority to make such a decision, saying the position of the Yang di-Pertuan Besar was governed by the state constitution and the Dewan Keadilan dan Undang (DKU), which has jurisdiction over customary matters involving the state ruler.
“An Exco decision cannot by itself override the Laws of the Constitution of Negeri Sembilan 1959 or the decisions of the Dewan Keadilan dan Undang Negeri Sembilan,” he said in a statement today.
Yesterday, the state Exco announced that it regarded an April 19 proclamation removing Tuanku Muhriz from the throne as valid and recognised Tuanku Nadzaruddin Tuanku Ja’afar as the new Yang di-Pertuan Besar with immediate effect.
Loke said Tuanku Muhriz could not be removed from the throne without going through the process required under the state constitution.
He also pointed out that the Exco members had only taken their oaths of office before Tuanku Muhriz in early August.
“If they now no longer recognise His Royal Highness as the Yang di-Pertuan Besar of Negeri Sembilan, then as a matter of principle and dignity, they should resign from their respective positions.”
Loke said the Exco’s announcement had caused confusion, disrupted the orderly administration of the state and undermined the dignity of the institution of the Yang di-Pertuan Besar.
He added that DAP remained committed to parliamentary democracy and constitutional monarchy, saying the rule of law and the dignity of the royal institution must be upheld.
The dispute dates back to April 19, when four individuals claiming to be Undangs announced the removal of Tuanku Muhriz, a declaration the DKU subsequently ruled had no legal effect under the Negeri Sembilan Constitution.
The DKU today reaffirmed that Tuanku Muhriz remains the legitimate Yang di-Pertuan Besar, saying there is no vacancy or successor and that the Exco’s September 16 decision to recognise his removal has no legal effect.

Title: Kedah fertiliser company managing director released on MACC bail
Article:
ALOR SETAR, Sept 17 — The Malaysian Anti-Corruption Commission (MACC) in Kedah has released the managing director of a fertiliser supplier company who was remanded in connection with the delay in the distribution of Supplementary Compound Fertiliser supplies to paddy farmers in the state.
According to MACC sources, the male suspect, in his 30s, was remanded for four days until yesterday and was released after his remand period ended.
The sources said, however, the suspect must report to the Kedah MACC office every month and must turn up if called upon to assist in the investigation.
Meanwhile, Kedah MACC director Datuk Nazli Rasyid Sulong, when contacted, confirmed the matter and said the suspect had been released on MACC bail.
Previously, the MACC opened an investigation paper regarding the issue of delayed distribution of Paddy Fertiliser 3 to paddy farmers in Kedah.
The investigation paper was opened following a complaint received from the Malaysian Paddy Farmers Brotherhood Organisation (PeSAWAH) on August 26 regarding the delay in fertiliser supply, which has affected the needs of paddy farmers in the Muda Agricultural Development Authority (MADA) area spanning 100,000 hectares. — Bernama

Title: Global energy shock now hitting Malaysia’s electricity costs, says economy minister
Article:
JOHOR BAHRU, Sept 17 — Global energy supply disruptions are now exhibiting a lagging effect, as the impact, concentrated on the petrol market since last March, begins to spread to natural gas and coal.
Economy Minister Akmal Nasrullah Mohd Nasir said the lagging effect is beginning to impact electricity generation costs directly, particularly for consumers whose monthly electricity usage exceeds 600 kilowatt-hours (kWh).
“We now see the impact has spread to other energy supplies, including the prices of natural gas, coal and others,” he said after presenting a mock cheque for the Johor Bahru Parliamentary constituency Health Clinic at Medan Niaga Kampung Melayu Majidee here today.
“The fluctuations affecting consumers using more than 600 kWh are based on fuel costs, known as the Automated Fuel Adjustment (AFA), which reflects fuel prices.
“That is the challenge we face because the lagging effect of the energy supply disruption, which began with petrol, is now increasingly being felt in other energy sectors, including natural gas, which usually takes three to four months before impacting current electricity tariffs,” he said.
“Natural gas is a fuel that is burned to generate energy. Its impact is now being observed on a global scale. Typically, when the price of petrol rises, there is a ‘lag effect’ — a delay of three to four months — before natural gas is affected.
“Today’s discussion is about July and August energy consumption. There is a retrospective impact, that is, the cost of the fuel we burn to generate electricity has risen,” he said.
Nonetheless, Akmal said the current tariff-setting mechanism is able to protect the majority of small-scale domestic consumers from being directly affected.
“There may be other aspects of the mechanism that Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim is reviewing that we can look into. Under the current tariff structure, most consumers using below 600 kWh are not directly affected in terms of the tariff position, or the supply price or fuel cost that we receive.
“We know that under the existing tariff structure, the tariff for those using below 600 kWh per month remains unchanged,” he said.
To address the knock-on effects of the global energy crisis, he said the Prime Minister will chair a special meeting to reassess the tariff situation to reduce people’s burden.
“I understand that the prime minister has said there is a need to convene a special meeting today to assess, evaluate and take into account the issues faced by the people,” he said.
He also pointed out that current unfavourable weather conditions were indirectly contributing to a rise in daily energy consumption.
“When the weather is unfavourable, we advise people to remain indoors in safer places, but this may also contribute to higher energy consumption,” he said. — Bernama

Title: First recipients praise new MyKad’s tougher security and sturdier design
Article:
PUTRAJAYA, Sept 17 — Members of the public have described the issuance of the new-generation MyKad, equipped with 53 security features and rolled out today, as a positive improvement in terms of technology and security, while also strengthening identity protection.
The new-generation MyKad, issued by the National Registration Department (NRD), is the seventh-generation identity card and has been upgraded from 23 to 53 modern, secure features to meet current needs.
Nineteen-year-old student Puteri Nur Syafiqah Jailani said she was excited to receive the new-generation MyKad on the first day of its issuance, describing the replacement process at NRD as easy and fast.
“Actually, I did not know that the new MyKad would be issued today. When I arrived at NRD, I saw a notice about the new MyKad.
“I immediately called my mother and was excited to have it. The security features are definitely better, and I also saw the announcement about the improved security features on TikTok,” she said.
Speaking to reporters here, she advised the public to make an appointment before going to NRD to facilitate the MyKad replacement process.
“If we have made an appointment, the process of getting a queue number is faster and the waiting time is not long,” said Puteri Nur Syafiqah, who lives in Putrajaya.
Shaza Nuizeaan Shafie, 48, from Puchong, Selangor, said the process of replacing the MyKad with the new-generation version was very easy and that the new card was also more attractive.
She said she went to the Putrajaya NRD to apply for identity cards for her two children - Nur Ataa Iqra Abdul Wahab, 21, and Nur Amnaa Irbah, 12.
“I made an appointment for 9.50am but arrived early. Alhamdulillah, the process was indeed fast, and the new MyKad is also very attractive. It has several new security features, which are very good for protecting the identity of the cardholder,” she said.
Forty-seven-year-old Khairul Anuar Azizan, meanwhile, praised NRD staff for handling the issuance of the new-generation MyKad quickly and efficiently.
“The process was really quick, and we did not have to wait for a long time. Many are excited about this new MyKad,” he said.
Private-sector employee Foo Yew Jin, 36, said the new-generation MyKad looked more secure and had more enhanced safety features.
“The card looks sturdier, so it may be harder to break. Perhaps it will be further improved and have more functions in the future,” he said.
On Tuesday (September 15), Home Minister Datuk Seri Saifuddin Nasution Ismail advised members of the public not to rush to replace their MyKad with the new version when applications opened today.
He said the replacement exercise for the new MyKad, which comes with about 50 additional security features, would be carried out in phases, while existing cards would remain valid for daily transactions.
Starting today, applications for the new-generation MyKad can be made at 40 NRD branches equipped with printing centres that can produce the cards on the same day.
At NRD branches without printing facilities, one can still apply for the new-generation MyKad, with the cards ready within five working days.
The new-generation MyKad incorporates security elements such as a Dynamic Security Hologram and Transparent Window on the front, as well as an Enforcement QR Code and a Dual-Interface Chip on the back. — Bernama

Title: Soldier charged with kicking five-year-old daughter at Kelantan eatery
Article:
KOTA BHARU, Sept 17 — A soldier was charged in the Sessions Court here today with abusing his five-year-old daughter by kicking her at an eatery in Jalan Kuala Krai last Friday.
Mohamed Nisa Mohamed Nasir, 40, pleaded not guilty after the charge was read out to him before Judge Zulkifli Abllah.
According to the charge, the accused allegedly kicked the girl at an eatery at Lot 143, Batu 2, Jalan Kuala Krai, here at 10.55pm on September 11, 2026.
The accused was charged under Section 31(1)(a) of the Child Act 2001, which is punishable under Section 31(1) of the same Act.
If convicted, he faces a fine of up to RM50,000 or imprisonment for up to 20 years, or both.
Earlier, the prosecution did not offer bail, citing concerns that the accused could interfere with the victim, who is also his biological daughter.
However, the defence requested bail, saying the accused had served in the military for 19 years and has three children.
The court was also told that his wife is unemployed and requires haemodialysis treatment, and that she relies on him to accompany her for regular hospital visits.
The defence also said the accused has no previous record of domestic violence offences or complaints and is not a flight risk as he is subject to the control of his military unit.
The court granted him bail of RM10,000 with one local surety, subject to several conditions, including that he must not interfere with any prosecution witnesses, particularly the victim.
He was also ordered to surrender his passport to the court, if he has one, and report to the Pengkalan Chepa Police Station or the nearest police station every two weeks until the case is concluded.
The court set October 22 for mention for the submission of documents. — Bernama

Title: Puchong blaze guts four factories, collapse risk remains (VIDEO)
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 17 — A fire destroyed four factories at Jalan TPP 5/15, Puchong Industrial Park, today.
Selangor Fire and Rescue Department (JBPM) assistant director of operations Ashrul Riezal Asbar said the department received an emergency call at 6.34am.
He said the fire affected a total area measuring 80 by 100 feet, involving four premises comprising a tyre factory, a hardware factory for pipes and valves, a furniture factory and an engineering factory.
“The fire was brought under control at 8.30am, while firefighting operations on the roofs and inside the factories are still underway. There is still a risk of the roofs and structures collapsing, but the spread of the fire remains under control,” he said in a statement.
Ashrul Riezal said the firefighting operation involved 33 personnel and 12 fire engines from the Puchong, Subang Jaya, Penchala, Petaling Jaya, Seri Kembangan and Cyberjaya stations.
He added that the cause and damage had yet to be determined. — Bernama

Title: BUDI Diesel mobile counters proposed for Sabah, Sarawak, says minister
Article:
KOTA KINABALU, Sept 17 — The BUDI Madani Diesel (BUDI Diesel) mobile counter programme has been proposed for expansion to Sabah and Sarawak to ensure rural and remote communities are not left out of the initiative’s enhanced benefits because of limited access to digital services.
Minister in the Prime Minister’s Department (Sabah and Sarawak) Datuk Mustapha Sakmud said the geographical realities of both states required an approach that brought services closer to the people rather than relying solely on online platforms.
“We should not rely solely on online portals. The geographical realities of Sabah and Sarawak, particularly for rural and remote communities, call for a more direct, hands-on approach.
“I propose expanding initiatives such as the BUDI Diesel Mobile Counter in collaboration with the Community Development Leader Unit (UPPM) in Sabah; Community Leaders and Chiefs (KMKK) and Village Development and Security Committees (JKKK) in Sarawak; as well as District Offices, the Ministry of Domestic Trade and Cost of Living (KPDN) and other relevant agencies,” he said in a statement today.
He said the approach was important to ensure that no citizen was left behind due to a lack of information, misunderstanding of application procedures or limited access to digital services.
Mustapha also urged the Ministry of Finance (MOF), KPDN and relevant agencies to strengthen cooperation with grassroots community leadership structures.
“This grassroots leadership network is closest to the community and can be leveraged to disseminate information, identify those in need of assistance and guide the public through the processes of eligibility checks, applications, appeals and the transfer of BUDI Diesel eligibility,” he said.
Mustapha said the improvements to the BUDI Diesel scheme announced yesterday by Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim were significant for Sabah and Sarawak as they took into account the realities of vehicle usage in both states.
Under the new ruling, registered owners can transfer their eligibility to any eligible actual user of a private diesel vehicle, effective immediately.
Owners of more than one private diesel vehicle can also transfer eligibility to up to three other individuals, subject to the stipulated conditions.
“I view these improvements as proof that the prime minister is listening to the voices of the people of Sabah and Sarawak.
“However, a good policy will only achieve its objectives when people at the grassroots level can benefit from the facilities provided,” he said.
Mustapha said feedback on the implementation of BUDI Diesel in Sabah and Sarawak would continue to be raised at Cabinet meetings to ensure the matter remained a priority for the federal government. — Bernama

Title: Bill requiring children to support ageing parents likely next year, says Kulasegaran
Article:
IPOH, Sept 17 — The proposed filial law that would legally require children to care for their ageing parents is still under consultation and is likely to be tabled early next year, Deputy Minister in the Prime Minister’s Department (Law and Institutional Reform) M. Kulasegaran said.
Kulasegaran said he had hoped the Bill could be tabled by October this year, but the timeframe was too short as the government still needed to consult non-governmental organisations, relevant departments and other stakeholders.
“I’m hoping for this year. But probably, it looks like early next year,” he told reporters after attending the Program Sumbangan Prihatin Hari Malaysia at Trends Restaurant here.
Kulasegaran also explained that the proposed law did not fall under the jurisdiction of the Law and Institutional Reform Ministry, but the ministry overseeing family and welfare matters, with his ministry collaborating on the matter.
He said the proposed Family Support Bill would address situations where elderly parents were no longer working while their adult children, including professionals such as lawyers, doctors, politicians and engineers, failed to provide financial or other support.
He said Malaysia had studied similar laws in countries including Singapore and India, where legislation allows parents who are not supported by their children to seek a court order requiring their children to provide financial support.
“This is not an unusual proposal. In several countries, including India, Singapore and others, we have studied what kind of legislation could be adopted in Malaysia,” he said.
Kulasegaran said the government could not introduce such legislation arbitrarily as it first needed to examine related laws and conduct various consultations before deciding on the appropriate course of action.
“The process has already been carried out and is ongoing,” he said, adding that he hoped the proposal could be brought forward despite the limited timeframe between October and December.
He said the need for such legislation had also been raised by elderly parents.
Kulasegaran also said he had observed that people who failed to care for their parents could later face similar difficulties when seeking care from their own children.
On mandatory caning, Kulasegaran said the matter was also still under consultation following an impact assessment meeting he chaired recently.
He said the government had received expert opinions and various recommendations on the matter on Tuesday, but could not disclose the details as they were covered under the Official Secrets Act.
“We have had discussions with the Attorney General’s Chambers and various other parties. I am in charge of the meeting,” he said.
Asked whether the abolition of caning was among the recommendations, Kulasegaran declined to comment.

Title: Kuantan businessman loses RM218,000 after 53 transactions in crypto scam
Article:
KUANTAN, Sept 17 — A senior citizen lost RM218,239.24 after he was believed to have fallen victim to a non-existent cryptocurrency investment scam advertised on social media.
Acting Pahang police chief Datuk Azry Akmar Ayob said the 65-year-old man, who runs a water filter business in Kuantan, came across a cryptocurrency investment offer on Facebook before joining a WhatsApp group last July.
“The victim was then given instructions to make an investment and was promised high returns based on the profits displayed through the Uphold application,” he said in a statement today.
After making 53 transactions through Luno, Mxglobal and Trust Wallet to the Uphold investment account, the victim’s Uphold account was frozen on Aug 20 and he was asked to pay RM30,000 as tax to activate it.
“However, the victim did not receive any returns as promised and was unable to withdraw the money,” he said, adding that the case is being investigated under Section 420 of the Penal Code.
Azry Akmar advised the public to be wary of investment offers promising high returns within a short period, especially those received through social media and messaging applications.
He said they should also check account and telephone numbers via the Semak Mule platform before making any financial transactions.
“Those who suspect they have fallen victim to a scam are urged to immediately contact the National Scam Response Centre (NSRC) at 997 or lodge a police report,” he said. — Bernama

Title: Sabah Marine Police seize untaxed cigarettes, liquor worth RM5.37m
Article:
KOTA KINABALU, Sept 17 — The Region 4 Sabah Marine Police (PPM) seized untaxed cigarettes and liquor worth nearly RM5.37 million in three raids in Sandakan and Kota Kinabalu early this week.
In a statement today, Region 4 Sabah PPM said the first raid was conducted at an unregistered jetty along the Seguntur River in Sandakan at about 1.30 am on Sept 15 as part of a special joint operation with the Malaysian Anti-Corruption Commission (MACC), following intelligence gathering.
The operation resulted in the arrest of a 45-year-old man and the seizure of 1.82 million sticks of cigarettes of various brands believed to have been smuggled from a neighbouring country, with an estimated value of RM2.564 million.
Acting on information obtained following the arrest and seizure, the raiding team subsequently located another speedboat hidden among mangrove trees along the Seguntur River.
An inspection of the boat uncovered 1.73 million sticks of cigarettes of various brands, with an estimated seizure value of RM2.326 million.
Meanwhile, in a separate operation on September 14, Region 4 Sabah PPM raided an unnumbered warehouse in Kampung Dambai, Jalan Tuaran Bypass, and seized 43,200 cans of liquor suspected to be untaxed, valued at RM478,506.
The case is being investigated under Sections 135(1)(d) and 135(1)(e) of the Customs Act 1967.
According to the statement, Region 4 Sabah PPM recorded 61 cases under the Customs Act 1967 between January and September 15 this year, involving seizures worth RM8,386,812.61 and 40 arrests.
The force said the latest success reflected the effectiveness of intelligence sharing and strategic cooperation with the MACC in strengthening enforcement efforts and combating the smuggling and distribution of untaxed goods.
It said enforcement operations would continue to be intensified, with greater emphasis on information sharing and inter-agency cooperation to curb smuggling activities. — Bernama

Title: Tuanku Muhriz remains legitimate Yamtuan, says Negeri Sembilan DKU
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 17 — The Dewan Keadilan dan Undang (DKU) Negeri Sembilan has reaffirmed that Tuanku Muhriz Tuanku Munawir remains the legitimate Yang di-Pertuan Besar of Negri Sembilan, saying there is no vacancy in the position and no successor while it is lawfully occupied.
In a statement today, the DKU also said the state executive council’s decision dated September 16 had no legal effect insofar as it purported to confirm Tuanku Muhriz’s removal, recognise a new ruler and order its immediate implementation.
It said such matters fell outside the jurisdiction of the state executive council and contradicted the binding determinations of the DKU under the Negeri Sembilan Constitution.
The statement came after two statements were issued following the DKU’s September 13 media statement, namely the Negeri Sembilan Menteri Besar’s statement dated September 15 and the document titled “Keputusan Majlis Mesyuarat Kerajaan Negeri Sembilan Bil. 6 Tahun 2026” dated September 16.
The DKU said it welcomed Menteri Besar Datuk Ismail Lasim’s September 15 statement, which maintained that the menteri besar had no unilateral power to terminate or vacate the office of Yang di-Pertuan Besar and that the validity and effect of the April 19 proclamation should be determined through lawful constitutional and legal processes, including judicial determination.
It said this position was consistent with the Negeri Sembilan Constitution and the DKU’s own determinations.
The DKU said questions involving Malay adat, including the election, appointment, resignation and removal of the Yang di-Pertuan Besar and Undang, fell within its jurisdiction under Article XVI of the state constitution.
It said Article XVI(3) further provided that the DKU’s advice on such matters was final and could not be challenged or questioned in any court on any grounds.
The DKU said the April 19 proclamation remained defective and void from the outset, as no enquiry under Article X(1) of the state constitution had been conducted, while three of its four signatories were not lawfully serving as Undang at the time.
It also said the function under Article X(2) had already been exercised after the menteri besar at the time refused to sign the proclamation, resulting in the proclamation lapsing and becoming void.
“The State Executive Council cannot cure these defects,” the statement said.
The DKU added that any proclamation purporting to elect a new Yang di-Pertuan Besar under Article XI would similarly be invalid as it was based on the same defective foundation and signed by people who did not lawfully hold the office of Undang.
It also said the prerogative of the Undang Yang Empat could only be exercised by Undang who lawfully held office and in accordance with the requirements and procedures prescribed by the state constitution.
The DKU said the matter was currently before the Seremban High Court and that a court order remained in force, urging all parties to respect the judicial process and refrain from taking steps that could circumvent or interfere with it.
It reiterated that Tuanku Muhriz remained the legitimate Yang di-Pertuan Besar and Yang di-Pertua of the DKU, adding that the institutions of Malay adat in Negri Sembilan, including those of the Yang di-Pertuan Besar and Undang, did not belong to any political party or individual but were a trust for all members of the community and their descendants.

Title: Masked gang steals up to RM1m in second robbery at Kedah goldsmith
Article:
SUNGAI PETANI, Sept 17 — Four masked men armed with hammers and sharp weapons robbed a goldsmith shop in Bakar Arang here yesterday, making off with jewellery worth between RM700,000 and RM1 million.
Kuala Muda Police chief ACP Hanyan Ramlan said police received a call at 7.20 pm alerting them to the incident at the shop located inside a supermarket here.
“Initial investigation found that the suspects arrived on two motorcycles. Two of them entered the shop while the other two waited outside.
“They smashed the display cases and took the items inside. The total losses are still being assessed, but preliminary estimates put the value at between RM700,000 and RM1 million,” he told reporters last night.
He said the same shop was also robbed in 2024, with losses estimated at RM1 million.
“The case is being investigated under Sections 395 and 397 of the Penal Code,” he added. — Bernama

Title: Perak worst hit as 28 areas nationwide turn unhealthy
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 17 — A total of 28 areas nationwide recorded Air Pollutant Index (API) readings at unhealthy levels as of 9.45am today.
According to the Malaysia Air Pollutant Index Management System (APIMS) portal, five areas in Perak recorded unhealthy readings, namely Tasek Ipoh (182), Seri Manjung (180), Pegoh Ipoh (160), Taiping (157) and Tanjung Malim (154).
In Penang, four areas recorded unhealthy readings, namely Seberang Jaya (156), Minden (156), Seberang Perai (154) and Balik Pulau (110), while Selangor also recorded four, namely Johan Setia (157), Shah Alam (154), Banting (144) and Petaling Jaya (135).
In Kuala Lumpur, unhealthy readings were recorded in Cheras (157) and Batu Muda (155), while Putrajaya recorded 157.
Negeri Sembilan recorded unhealthy readings in Nilai (157) and Seremban (151), while Melaka had three areas, namely Bukit Rambai (148), Bandaraya Melaka (133) and Alor Gajah (111).
In Johor, the affected areas were Batu Pahat (152) and Kluang (144), while Kedah recorded unhealthy readings in Sungai Petani (160) and Kulim Hi-Tech (132).
Meanwhile, three other states each recorded one unhealthy area, namely Kuala Terengganu (153) in Terengganu, Jerantut (152) in Pahang and Kuching (109) in Sarawak.
In addition, 32 areas nationwide recorded readings at moderate levels, while eight areas recorded good readings.
An API reading of zero to 50 indicates good air quality, 51 to 100 (moderate), 101 to 200 (unhealthy), 201 to 300 (very unhealthy) and 301 and above (hazardous). — Bernama

Title: Police probe 14-year-old driver after he crashes into two cars in Perai
Article:
BUKIT MERTAJAM, Sept 17 — Police have confirmed a viral video showing a 14-year-old boy driving a car and crashing into two vehicles at two separate locations in Taman Chai Leng, Perai, here.
Seberang Perai Tengah (SPT) district police chief ACP Nik Aminuddin Raja Abdullah said the incidents occurred at 4.50pm Tuesday, and a report was lodged at 8.47pm on the same day.
“Preliminary investigations found that the teenager, who was driving from Lorong Kurau 23 towards Jalan Kurau 1, first crashed into a car parked on the road shoulder.
“He then continued driving before allegedly entering the wrong side of a one-way road at Lebuh Kurau 5 and crashing into another car travelling in the correct lane,” he said in a statement last night.
Nik Aminuddin said the two accidents resulted in damage to all three vehicles, but no injuries were reported.
He said further investigations are ongoing and the case is being investigated under Section 42(1) of the Road Transport Act 1987 for reckless and dangerous driving.
He advised parents and guardians to monitor their children’s activities and not allow underage children to drive vehicles, as doing so is not only against the law but could also endanger other road users.
The public are also advised against speculating about the incident and to leave the investigation to the police.
Earlier, a video of the incident went viral on social media, showing a teenager driving a car and crashing into a vehicle before being stopped by members of the public at the scene. — Bernama

Title: Health Ministry denies claims officials absent from funerals of FDS crash victims
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 17 — Allegations that no senior health officials attended the funerals of members of the Flying Doctors Service (FDS) killed in a crash in Sarawak are untrue and irresponsible, Health deputy director-general Dr Ismuni Bohari said.
He added that he himself had visited the families of the crash victims in Miri and Kuching, and also paid his last respects to the victims.
“I myself was there, visiting the victims’ families in Miri and Kuching on behalf of Health Minister Datuk Seri Dr Dzulkefly Ahmad and the ministry’s senior leaders and paid my last respects to my beloved FDS colleagues.
“Dr Dzulkefly, secretary-general Datuk Seri Hasnol Zam Zam Ahmad and deputy secretary-general went to Senawang and I myself went to Miri and Kuching. That was what was determined by senior health officials,” he posted on X.
He said his presence was not only in an official capacity, but also out of humanitarian concern and his close ties with the FDS team, which he had previously been part of, as well as in his capacity as a Sarawak native and National Public Health Programme director.
“May we continue to honour those who have passed away and stand together in providing support and strength to the bereaved families,” he said.
Tuesday, a news portal alleged that the Health Minister should have paid his last respects to the families of the FDS victims in Sarawak instead of attending a conference in the capital while the victims’ funerals were being held.
Dr Ismuni said the news portal should have verified the facts and corrected the information in its report before legal action is taken. — Bernama

Title: Malaysians in Saudi Arabia told to remain calm, follow instructions amid emergency alerts
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 17 — Malaysians who receive alerts through Saudi Arabia’s National Early Warning Platform are advised to remain calm, stay vigilant and strictly follow instructions issued by Saudi authorities.
The Consulate General of Malaysia in Jeddah also advised Malaysians to take appropriate safety precautions upon receiving an emergency alert.
“…including remaining indoors where possible, staying away from windows and open areas, seeking immediate shelter when outdoors, avoiding crowded or potentially unsafe locations, and continuing to monitor official announcements,” the consulate general said in a safety advisory posted on Facebook on Wednesday.
In case of an emergency, they can contact 911 for the Makkah and Madinah regions or 998 for other parts of the Kingdom.
Malaysians who require emergency consular assistance can contact the consulate general at +966 57 309 9589.
“The Malaysian community is strongly encouraged not to panic or circulate unverified information. Please rely only on information and instructions issued by the relevant official authorities,” the advisory read.
Saudi Arabia on Tuesday issued emergency alerts warning of a “potential danger” in Jeddah, Makkah and Taif through its National Early Warning Platform for Emergencies, amid heightened tensions with the Houthi group.
Saudi air defences intercepted and destroyed a drone launched by the Houthi group near Makkah on Tuesday, international media reported. — Bernama

Title: MCA ready for GE16, focus not on number of seats, says Wee
Article:
YONG PENG, Sept 17 — MCA president Datuk Seri Wee Ka Siong yesterday declared that the party is at a high level of readiness to face the 16th general election (GE16).
The Ayer Hitam MP said MCA has been preparing early to face the election and did not leave things to the last minute, adding that elections could be called at any time because administrations usually last between three years eight months and over four years, based on the last 15 general elections.
“So I feel at this time, there’s only several months left. Maybe four to five months. If we want it expedited, I think usually that will happen, doesn’t reach five years,” he said during a media conference after attending MCA’s annual Johor conference 2026 at Dewan Persatuan Vhe Ann Khor here yesterday.
He downplayed the number of seats MCA aimed to contest in GE16, stating that it was not the main issue.
“To me, the total isn’t important. To win more, that’s even better. But it’s only self gratification if we contest 50 seats and lost all of them, it’s pointless. For me, our target is to win,” he said.
On Kluang Umno’s proposal that MCA give way for Umno to contest the Kluang parliamentary seat for GE16, Wee said it could be discussed at the grassroots level, but the final decision would be at the Barisan Nasional (BN) leadership.
It would also be the same for any change or swapping of seats in other areas, he pointed out.
“What’s more important is that if BN places a candidate, that’s the candidate who represents BN,” he said. — Bernama

Title: Sarawak gets RM1.5b interim special grant as talks continue on annual formula, says Anwar
Article:
KUCHING, Sept 17 — Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim yesterday announced an increase in Sarawak’s interim special grant to RM1.5 billion, up from RM600 million previously, effective this year.
He said the Federal Government will continue negotiations with the Sabah and Sarawak state governments to finalise a sustainable formula for determining the annual Special Grant rate.
“Previously, I announced an increase from RM600 million to RM1.5 billion for Sabah.
“In the spirit of solidarity, friendship and the spirit of Malaysia, tonight I announce RM1.5 billion for Sarawak as well; this is the result of friendship and good negotiations,” he said at the national-level Malaysia Day 2026 celebrations at the Borneo Convention Centre Kuching (BCCK) here last night.
The Yang Dipertua Negeri of Sarawak, Tun Dr Wan Junaidi Tuanku Jaafar, was the guest of honour at the celebration.
Also present were Sarawak Premier Tan Sri Abang Johari Tun Openg and Sabah Chief Minister Datuk Seri Hajiji Noor.
Commenting on issues arising within the Malaysian federation, Anwar said there was no problem that could not be resolved and settled.
“I am grateful that through this spirit (of the Malaysian federation), we have been able to implement various projects and programmes for the benefit of the people,” he said.
Meanwhile, Anwar said he wanted national oil and gas company Petroliam Nasional Bhd (Petronas) and Petroleum Sarawak Bhd (Petros) to work together as a team to develop the nation.
He explained that to reach a consensus, both parties must respect and recognise rights and laws at both the state and federal levels.
“We have decided that the commercial agreement between Petronas and Petros must be expedited and finalised. There is no reason why this cannot be resolved,” he said. — Bernama
